author: copilot
body:
Implements a zero-dependency, GitHub Pages–compatible web app that calculates the f-number at which a camera sensor becomes diffraction-limited (N_critical).

## Architecture

Follows the [barjak-keyboard](https://github.com/lbarjak/barjak-keyboard) conventions: one class per file, `export default class`, arrow-function class methods, `<script type="module">` entry point, no bundler.

- **`src/sensordata.js`** — static list of 12 preset cameras
- **`src/calculator.js`** — `pixel_pitch = sensor_width / sqrt(MP × 1e6 × aspect)`, then `N_critical = pixel_pitch / (1.22 × 0.00055)`
- **`src/menu.js`** — two-step UI: preset picker → or custom sensor dimensions form
- **`src/display.js`** — results grid + log₂-scaled f/1–f/22 bar with green (sharp) / red (diffraction-limited) zones
- **`src/app.js`** — wires menu → calculator → display, handles back-navigation
- **`index.html`** — dark theme, inline `<style>`, responsive to mobile

## Screenshots

**Camera selection & results (Sony A7II, N_critical = f/8.8):**

![Camera selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10a1ebf8-c324-4ab4-8a76-eef032183433)
![Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f913520-d223-4422-a7bc-15cd922b4f4d)

**Edge case — N_critical < f/1 (Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra 200 MP, fully diffraction-limited at any practical aperture):**

![Edge case](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d8d069c-48dd-42fd-832e-994f8cef5e22)

**Custom sensor input:**

![Custom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bbc2738-fcf8-4125-b740-cb780e7c58f3)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> Create a browser-based diffraction limit calculator application. The app should be a vanilla JavaScript application using ES6 classes, following the coding style of https://github.com/lbarjak/barjak-keyboard — specifically:
> 
> - **One class per file**, filename matches class name (lowercase)
> - `export default class ClassName` pattern
> - `<script type="module">` in index.html
> - No bundler, no framework — pure vanilla JS running in browser
> - Arrow function class methods (like `methodName = () => { }`)
> - Files in `src/` directory, `index.html` in root
> 
> ## Application functionality
> 
> A **Diffraction Limit Calculator** that helps photographers understand at which f-number their camera sensor becomes diffraction-limited.
> 
> ### Step-by-step menu flow:
> 
> 1. **Choose camera**: Either select a preset camera or choose "Custom" to enter parameters manually
> 2. **If preset**: Auto-fills sensor dimensions and megapixels
> 3. **If custom**: User enters sensor width (mm), sensor height (mm), and megapixels
> 4. **Display results**: Shows the diffraction limit (N_critical) with a visual f-stop scale
> 
> ### Calculation:
> 
> ```
> pixel_pitch = sensor_width / horizontal_pixels
> horizontal_pixels = sqrt(megapixels * 1000000 * (sensor_width / sensor_height))
> N_critical = pixel_pitch / (1.22 × λ)     where λ = 0.00055 mm (550nm green light)
> Airy_disk = 2.44 × λ × N
> ```
> 
> ### Preset cameras to include:
> 
> | Name | Sensor Width (mm) | Sensor Height (mm) | Megapixels |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Doogee V31 GT (50MP) | 5.7 | 4.28 | 50 |
> | Doogee V31 GT (12.5MP binned) | 5.7 | 4.28 | 12.5 |
> | Olympus Stylus 1 | 7.44 | 5.58 | 12 |
> | Sony RX100 | 13.2 | 8.8 | 20.2 |
> | Sony A7II (Full Frame) | 35.8 | 23.9 | 24.3 |
> | Sony A7II (APS-C crop) | 23.5 | 15.6 | 10.3 |
> | Sony A7RIV (Full Frame) | 35.7 | 23.8 | 61 |
> | Canon EOS R5 | 36.0 | 24.0 | 45 |
> | Nikon Z9 | 35.9 | 23.9 | 45.7 |
> | Fujifilm X-T5 (APS-C) | 23.5 | 15.6 | 40.2 |
> | iPhone 15 Pro (Main) | 9.8 | 7.3 | 48 |
> | Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (Main) | 9.8 | 7.3 | 200 |
> 
> ### File structure:
> 
> ```
> index.html          — Main HTML, inline CSS, <script type="module"> entry point
> src/
>   app.js            — App class: entry point, orchestration
>   sensordata.js     — SensorData class: preset camera data, static data store
>   calculator.js     — Calculator class: diffraction calculations (N_critical, pixel pitch, Airy disk)
>   menu.js           — Menu class: UI menu handling (preset selection, custom input forms)
>   display.js        — Display class: result visualization, f-stop scale bar
> README.md           — Documentation with formula explanation and GitHub Pages link
> ```
> 
> ### Display/Results section should show:
> 
> - Camera name (or "Custom")
> - Sensor dimensions
> - Megapixels
> - Calculated pixel pitch (µm)
> - **N_critical (the diffraction limit f-number)**
> - A **visual f-stop scale bar** from f/1.0 to f/22 with a marker showing where diffraction limiting begins
> - Green zone (below N_critical = sharp) and red zone (above = diffraction limited)
> - Text: "Diffraction limited beyond **f/X.X**"
> 
> ### Styling:
> 
> - Clean, modern, dark theme (dark background, light text)
> - Responsive — works on mobile and desktop
> - No external CSS frameworks
> - Inline styles in index.html `<style>` block (same pattern as barjak-keyboard)
> 
> ### GitHub Pages demo:
> 
> - The app must work when served from GitHub Pages (github.io)
> - All paths must be relative
> - Include a README.md explaining the app, the formula, and linking to the GitHub Pages demo at `https://lbarjak.github.io/diffraction-limit-calculator/`
> 
> ### README.md should include:
>

## Root cause
- Render deploy logs still failed with `Config validation error: "TLS_KEY" is required` after PR #73 merged.
- The Render service environment is configured with `TSL_KEY`, `TSL_CERT`, and `TSL_PORT` instead of `TLS_*`.

- keep canonical `TLS_*` names preferred when both are present
- add regression coverage for config loading and production env validation

author: xutizhou
body:
## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

In DeepSeek V3/R1 with expert parallelism (EP), each rank currently computes the shared expert **separately** from routed experts. This means shared expert is not part of the DeepEP dispatch/compute/combine pipeline — it runs as a standalone forward pass on every rank.

This PR fuses the shared expert into the MoE path by treating it as an additional routed expert (the "9th expert" per rank). Instead of computing shared expert separately, it is dispatched through DeepEP alongside routed experts, assigned to the source rank's local shared expert slot.

This is the **first half** of the waterfill feature split (requested by @ch-wan in #19290):
- **[1/2] This PR**: Fuse shared expert into DeepEP dispatch (fixed local assignment)
- **[2/2] Follow-up PR**: Add waterfill load balancing to dynamically assign shared expert to the least-loaded rank

coauthor: @AichenF

## Modifications

**New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/deepep_shared_expert_fusion.py`** (65 lines)
- `LOCAL_SHARED_MARKER`: sentinel value for invalid expert ID (DeepEP ignores `expert_id < 0`)
- `expand_topk_with_shared_expert()`: expands topk output `[N, 8] → [N, 9]` with expert ID remapping and shared expert always assigned to source rank

**Modified files:**

- **`models/deepseek_v2.py`** (+138/−22):
  - Adjusts `num_experts` and `top_k` to account for extra shared expert slots (`+ep_size` experts, `+1` topk)
  - Skips standalone shared expert forward when fusion is enabled
  - Calls `expand_topk_with_shared_expert()` after TopK selection to append shared expert column
  - Allows shared expert fusion under EP when `--enable-deepep-waterfill` is set (bypasses existing EP disable checks)

- **`layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`** (+40/−2):
  - Expert ID remapping in weight loading: maps checkpoint expert IDs to expanded layout (original routed experts + 1 shared expert slot per rank)
  - Adjusts shared expert detection threshold for the expanded expert ID space

- **`server_args.py`** (+29/−1):
  - Adds `--enable-deepep-waterfill` CLI flag with validation (requires `moe_a2a_backend='deepep'`)
  - Updates `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` help text

## Usage

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path <DeepSeek-V3-path> \
    --tp 16 --dp-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0|1} \
    --dist-init-addr <addr>:<port> \
    --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
    --enable-dp-attention \
    --enable-deepep-waterfill
```

## Benchmarking and Profiling

author: avifenesh
body:
## Summary

Implements lightweight Producer class for serverless/edge environments (AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions) where persistent connections are expensive or impossible.

### Key Changes

- **Producer class** - Fire-and-forget job enqueueing without EventEmitter overhead
  - Returns string job IDs (not Job instances)
  - Supports both ephemeral and pooled clients
  - Reuses battle-tested addJob/dedup FCALL functions
  - API: `add()`, `addBulk()`, `close()`

- **ServerlessPool** - Connection reuse for warm invocations
  - Caches Producer instances by queue name + connection fingerprint
  - Module-level singleton for convenient use
  - API: `getProducer()`, `closeAll()`, `size`

- **Documentation** - Comprehensive serverless guide
  - docs/SERVERLESS.md with AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge examples
  - README.md updated with serverless section
  - CHANGELOG.md entries for v0.8.1

### Implementation Details

- No breaking changes - Producer is a new export
- Zero new Lua code - reuses existing Queue functions
- Batched cross-queue parent registrations (O(1) vs O(N) round trips)
- Consistent GlideMQError usage throughout
- Compression included in pool fingerprint to prevent cache collisions

### Test Coverage

- 58 tests total (29 standalone + 29 cluster mode)
- Tests for Producer.add(), addBulk(), close()
- Tests for ServerlessPool caching and lifecycle
- Integration tests (Producer + Worker)

author: yixinshark
body:
When KWin's screenshot service encounters an internal error, it may hold the write end of the pipe open without writing any data and without closing it. In this case, the previous blocking `QFile::read()` would wait forever, hanging the taskbar process.

Three issues are fixed in fetchWindowPreview():

1. Replace `pipe()` with `pipe2(fd, O_CLOEXEC)` to prevent the write fd from being inherited by child processes, which would also cause read() to block indefinitely.

2. Replace the blocking `QFile::read()` with a `poll()`-based read loop with a 5-second timeout. If KWin stalls or the pipe produces no data within the timeout, the function aborts gracefully and returns an empty QPixmap instead of hanging.

3. Fix the read buffer size calculation: use `imageHeight * imageStride` instead of `imageWidth * imageHeight * bpp / 8`. imageStride is the actual bytes-per-row (including alignment padding) as reported by KWin, and may be larger than width * bpp/8. The old calculation could result in reading too few bytes, leading to an out-of-bounds access when constructing QImage. Also added image.copy() to ensure the QImage owns its data independently of the fileContent buffer.

当 KWin 截图服务发生内部异常时，可能持有管道写端却不写入任何数据
也不关闭，导致原先的阻塞式 `QFile::read()` 永久等待，任务栏进程卡死。

本次修复了 fetchWindowPreview() 中的三个问题：

1. 将 `pipe()` 改为 `pipe2(fd, O_CLOEXEC)`，防止写端 fd 被 fork 出的子进程继承，否则子进程持有写端也会导致 read() 永久阻塞。

2. 将阻塞式 `QFile::read()` 替换为带 5 秒超时的 `poll()` 读取循环。 若 KWin 卡顿或管道在超时内无数据，函数会提前退出并返回空的 QPixmap，而不是使进程永久挂起。

3. 修正读取缓冲区大小计算：使用 `imageHeight * imageStride` 而非 `imageWidth * imageHeight * bpp / 8`。imageStride 是 KWin 返回的 每行实际字节数（含内存对齐 padding），可能大于 width*bpp/8。 原来的计算会导致读取字节数偏小，在构造 QImage 时发生越界访问。 同时添加 image.copy() 确保 QImage 独立持有数据。

Log: prevent indefinite blocking in fetchWindowPreview pipe read

## Summary by Sourcery

Prevent window preview fetching from hanging when reading from the KWin screenshot pipe and ensure image data is fully and safely read.

Bug Fixes:
- Avoid indefinite blocking when reading from the KWin screenshot pipe by adding a timeout-based polling loop.
- Fix incorrect read buffer sizing for window preview images to prevent out-of-bounds access and incomplete image data.

Enhancements:
- Use close-on-exec pipes for the KWin screenshot communication channel to avoid file descriptor leaks into child processes.
- Ensure QImage used for window previews owns its data via a deep copy before creating the pixmap.

author: penberg
body:
Adds `defaultQueryTimeout` connection option and per-query `{ queryTimeout: ms }` parameter to interrupt long-running queries via sqlite3_interrupt(). Available on exec(), run(), get(), iterate(), and all() in both sync and async APIs.

A shared background tokio task manages deadlines with a min-heap. Registering a query returns a TimeoutGuard — if the deadline expires before the guard is dropped, the connection is interrupted. Dropping the guard early (query completed) cancels the timeout and wakes the background task to release the connection reference immediately.

author: windoliver
body:
## Summary

Fixes 6 valid findings from codex review batch 3:

1. **scheduler-provider**: `cancel()` now verifies task ownership via `scheduler.query({ agentId })` before allowing cancellation. Documents limitation for `unschedule/pause/resume` (no schedule lookup in L0 contract).

2. **tool-browser**: Adds ref-counting for backend disposal — `detach()` only calls `backend.dispose()` when the last agent detaches, preventing premature disposal in multi-agent scenarios.

3. **lsp**: Adds ref-counting so `detach()` only closes LSP clients when the last attached agent leaves. Documents single-agent design.

4. **skills**: Guards against multi-agent misuse — throws if a second agent with a different ID tries to `attach()` to a provider already bound to another agent. Documents single-agent design.

5. **tools-web**: Normalizes fetch cache keys via `new URL(url).href` to prevent encoding-based dedup bypass. Documents DNS rebinding limitation in `url-policy.ts`.

6. **tool-ask-guide**: Sets `truncated: true` when the first (and only) result exceeds the token budget, so callers know the budget was exceeded even though the result is still included.

Findings verified as **INVALID** (not fixed):
- Scheduler semaphore leak: `finally { semaphore.release() }` guarantees release
- Catalog `get()` error collapsing: `fanOut()` preserves errors via `sourceErrors`

## Summary

Implements the Proton Mail connector (#127) that enables agents to send and read emails through a user's Proton Mail account via Proton Mail Bridge.

- `protonmail.send_email` (high risk) — send via SMTP with STARTTLS
- `protonmail.read_inbox` (low risk) — fetch recent emails via IMAP

- `protonmail.read_email` (low risk) — fetch full email by sequence number

- Email header injection prevention via `sanitizeHeaderValue()`
- Email address validation using `net/mail.ParseAddress`
- STARTTLS for SMTP connections
- `BODY[].PEEK` to avoid marking as read

## Test plan

- [x] 38 unit tests covering credential validation, parameter validation, send with mock SMTP, header injection prevention, email format validation
- [ ] Integration tests with real Proton Mail Bridge (requires running Bridge instance)

Closes #127

author: damiaocastro
body:
## Summary
This PR adds native notebook support to the BigQuery extension, allowing users to create and execute BigQuery SQL queries in VS Code notebooks with formatted result output.

## Key Changes
- **New Notebook Controller** (`bqNotebookController.ts`): Implements the core notebook execution engine that:
  - Executes BigQuery SQL queries from notebook cells
  - Polls job status until completion
  - Handles both single queries and BigQuery scripts with multiple child jobs
  - Renders query results as formatted HTML tables
  - Displays appropriate messages for DML/DDL statements with affected row counts
  - Provides error handling with detailed error output

- **New Notebook Serializer** (`bqNotebookSerializer.ts`): Handles persistence of notebook files (`.bqnb` format) by:
  - Deserializing JSON notebook files into VS Code notebook format
  - Serializing notebook data back to JSON with cell metadata
  - Supporting both code and markdown cell types

- **Extension Integration** (`extension.ts`): Registers the notebook type and wires up:
  - Notebook serializer for the `bqnb` type
  - Notebook controller for query execution
  - Proper subscription management for cleanup

- **Package Configuration** (`package.json`): Adds:
  - `onNotebook:bqnb` activation event
  - Notebook type definition with `.bqnb` file pattern association

## Notable Implementation Details
- Query results are rendered as styled HTML tables with alternating row colors and monospace font
- Script jobs are handled by fetching child jobs, sorting them by execution order, and displaying results for each statement
- Proper HTML escaping prevents injection vulnerabilities in output rendering
- Job polling uses 1-second intervals to check for completion status
- Error handling distinguishes between job-level errors and execution exceptions

author: psihius
body:
## 📌 What Does This PR Do?

Stops `align-assignment-like` from padding compact inline arrays into columns.

Before this change, enabling `align-assignment-like` could turn:

```php
['status' => 'error', 'data' => $data]
```

into:

```php
['status' => 'error', 'data'   => $data]
```

This PR keeps that compact inline form unchanged, while still allowing alignment for multiline or width-broken mappings.

## 🔍 Context & Motivation

`align-assignment-like` already aligns useful grouped constructs, but it also affected compact inline arrays in ways that added noise without improving readability.

This change narrows the behavior so compact inline arrays stay compact, while meaningful multiline mappings still align.

## 🛠️ Summary of Changes

- limit array key/value alignment to arrays that are already multiline or exceed `print-width`
- keep compact inline arrays unaligned
- add regression coverage for compact inline arrays vs multiline mappings
- update the setting docs to describe the narrower behavior

## 📂 Affected Areas

- [x] Formatter
- [x] Tests
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Linter
- [ ] Analyzer
- [ ] CLI behavior unrelated to formatting

## 🔗 Related Issues or PRs

- bugfix for `align-assignment-like` array behavior

Focused formatter tests:
- `cargo test -p mago-formatter align_array_like -- --exact`

author: limbonaut
body:
The `sentry_log_trace/debug/info/...` convenience functions in sentry-native treat the body as a printf format string. If the log message contains format specifiers like `%s` or `%n` without corresponding arguments, this causes undefined behavior — and a guaranteed crash on Windows due to MSVC's CRT invalid parameter handler (`_invoke_watson`).

- Fixes #576
- Depends on https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-native/pull/1566

Switches to `sentry_log()` which takes the level as a parameter and doesn't interpret the body as a format string. Also adds a `_log_level_to_native()` helper for the level conversion.

author: touwaeriol
body:
## 背景 / Background

当前 API Key 账号仅支持设置总额度限制（`quota_limit`），缺乏周期性（日/周）配额维度。用户需要更灵活的配额控制——例如设置每日限额防止短时间内消耗过多，或设置周限额进行周期性预算管理。

Currently API Key accounts only support a total quota limit (`quota_limit`), lacking periodic (daily/weekly) quota dimensions. Users need more flexible quota controls — e.g., daily limits to prevent excessive consumption in short periods, or weekly limits for periodic budget management.

---

## 目的 / Purpose

为 API Key 账号新增日限额和周限额两个独立维度，与现有总限额共存。三个维度可独立配置，任一维度超限即暂停账号调度。日/周限额采用滚动周期+懒重置机制（周期过期后在下次计费时自动重置为 0），无需后台定时任务。

Add daily and weekly quota limit dimensions to API Key accounts, coexisting with the existing total quota limit. All three dimensions are independently configurable; exceeding any one pauses account scheduling. Daily/weekly limits use rolling periods with lazy reset (automatically reset to zero on next billing after period expiry), requiring no background cron jobs.

---

## 改动内容 / Changes

### 后端 / Backend

- **新增 Account 方法**：`GetQuotaDailyLimit/Used`、`GetQuotaWeeklyLimit/Used`、`HasAnyQuotaLimit`、`getExtraFloat64`、`getExtraTime`、`isPeriodExpired`
- **重写 `IsQuotaExceeded`**：检查总/日/周三个维度，任一超限返回 true
- **重写 `IncrementQuotaUsed` SQL**：原子更新三维度用量，日/周额度在周期过期时自动重置（inline UPDATE 避免 CTE 快照在 READ COMMITTED 下丢失更新）
- **重写 `ResetQuotaUsed` SQL**：重置所有维度用量并删除周期时间戳
- **`postUsageBilling`**：条件从 `GetQuotaLimit() > 0` 改为 `HasAnyQuotaLimit()`
- **`admin_service.go`**：编辑账号时保留 `quota_daily_used/start`、`quota_weekly_used/start` 避免意外重置

---

- **New Account methods**: `GetQuotaDailyLimit/Used`, `GetQuotaWeeklyLimit/Used`, `HasAnyQuotaLimit`, `getExtraFloat64`, `getExtraTime`, `isPeriodExpired`
- **Rewrite `IsQuotaExceeded`**: checks total/daily/weekly — any dimension exceeding returns true
- **Rewrite `IncrementQuotaUsed` SQL**: atomically updates 3 dimensions; daily/weekly auto-reset on period expiry (inline UPDATE to avoid CTE snapshot lost-update under READ COMMITTED)
- **Rewrite `ResetQuotaUsed` SQL**: resets all dimensions and removes period timestamps
- **`postUsageBilling`**: condition changed from `GetQuotaLimit() > 0` to `HasAnyQuotaLimit()`
- **`admin_service.go`**: preserve `quota_daily_used/start`, `quota_weekly_used/start` on account edit

### 前端 / Frontend

- **`QuotaLimitCard.vue`**：从单一 `v-model` 改为三个独立 props（`totalLimit`/`dailyLimit`/`weeklyLimit`），支持同时配置多个维度
- **新增 `QuotaBadge.vue`**：通用配额徽章组件，显示 `$used/$limit` 及颜色状态（绿/黄/红）
- **`AccountCapacityCell.vue`**：使用 `QuotaBadge` 显示 D（日）/W（周）/$（总）三维度徽章
- **`EditAccountModal.vue` / `CreateAccountModal.vue`**：新增日/周配额输入字段
- **`AccountActionMenu.vue`**：`hasQuotaLimit` 检查扩展为三维度
- **i18n**：新增日/周/总配额的标签和提示文案（中英文）

---

- **`QuotaLimitCard.vue`**: refactored from single `v-model` to 3 independent props (`totalLimit`/`dailyLimit`/`weeklyLimit`), supporting simultaneous multi-dimension configuration
- **New `QuotaBadge.vue`**: reusable quota badge component showing `$used/$limit` with color-coded status (green/yellow/red)
- **`AccountCapacityCell.vue`**: uses `QuotaBadge` to display D(daily)/W(weekly)/$(total) dimension badges
- **`EditAccountModal.vue` / `CreateAccountModal.vue`**: added daily/weekly quota input fields
- **`AccountActionMenu.vue`**: `hasQuotaLimit` check extended to three dimensions
- **i18n**: added labels and hints for daily/weekly/total quota (zh + en)

---

## 技术细节 / Technical Details

### 懒重置机制 / Lazy Reset Mechanism

日/周配额不使用后台定时任务重置，而是在 `IncrementQuotaUsed` SQL 中内联处理：
- 检查 `quota_daily_start` + 24h 是否 <= NOW()
- 如果已过期：重置 `quota_daily_used = $amount`，更新 `quota_daily_start` 为当前 UTC 时间
- 如果未过期：累加 `quota_daily_used += $amount`
- 周配额同理（168h 周期）
- 使用 inline UPDATE（非 CTE）避免 PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED 隔离级别下的并发丢失更新

Daily/weekly quotas use inline lazy reset in `IncrementQuotaUsed` SQL instead of background cron:
- Check if `quota_daily_start` + 24h <= NOW()
- If expired: reset `quota_daily_used = $amount`, update `quota_daily_start` to current UTC
- If not expired: accumulate `quota_daily_used += $amount`
- Weekly quota uses same logic with 168h period
- Uses inline UPDATE (not CTE) to avoid lost-update under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED isolation

author: virrius
body: Tool build logic has been reorganized All transformations, imports, and configuration assembly have been moved to the first stage at the model validator level. This allows us to fail fast if there are issues and centrally validate the input configuration before the agent is built at runtime. The factory has been simplified. The agent, tools, and other components now use a unified ToolDefinition data model and are no longer aware of the multi-level configuration or other related complexities. The number of dictionaries / non-validated non-model data structures in the agent and tool logic stages has been reduced. Search has been moved to the tool configuration level, and the related parts in the documentation have been fixed. Additional tests have been added for these cases. --- Упорядочена логика сборки тулов - все преобразования, импорты и составление конфига вынесены на первый этап на уровень валидаторов модели. Что позволяет нам быстро падать в случае проблем и централизованно валидировать входную конфигурацию прежде чем агент будет собран в рантайме - Упрощена фабрика - Агент, тулы и далее используют единообразную модель данных ToolDefinition, ничего не знают про многоуровневый конфиг и любые прочие проблемы - Сокращено количество словарей/невалидированных немодельных данных на этапах логики агентов и тулов Search\ перенесён на уровень конфигурации тулов, пофикшены эти моменты в документации Добавлены дополнительные тесты на эти кейсы

`sandbox_triggerpattern/cheatsheets/sandbox-hint-getting-started.xml` is the reference for the XML format and style. It is registered in `sandbox_triggerpattern/plugin.xml` under the `org.eclipse.ui.cheatsheets.cheatSheetContent` extension point. The `cheatsheets/` folder is included in `build.properties` via `bin.includes`.

## Plugins That Need Cheatsheets

For each plugin below, create the cheatsheet XML, register it in plugin.xml, and add the `cheatsheets/` folder to `build.properties`.

### 1. `sandbox_encoding_quickfix` — "Using the Explicit Encoding Cleanup"
- **plugin.xml**: `sandbox_encoding_quickfix/plugin.xml` — add `org.eclipse.ui.cheatsheets.cheatSheetContent` extension
- **build.properties**: `sandbox_encoding_quickfix/build.properties` — add `cheatsheets/` to `bin.includes`

  2. Enable the cleanup (Source → Clean Up → Configure → "Explicit Encoding (Sandbox)")
  3. Select encoding behavior mode (KEEP_BEHAVIOR vs ENFORCE_UTF8)
  4. Run the cleanup on a Java file
  5. Review the changes (e.g., `new FileReader(f)` → `new FileReader(f, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)`)

### 2. `sandbox_junit_cleanup` — "Migrating JUnit 4 to JUnit 5"

### 3. `sandbox_jface_cleanup` — "Modernizing JFace Code"

author: rubberduck203
body:
## Summary

- **Log-type-aware filenames**: ADIF exports now use a format that matches each log type's upload convention instead of the generic `duklog-` prefix:
  - POTA: `{CALLSIGN}@{PARK}-{YYYYMMDD}.adif` — matches the POTA email submission requirement
  - General: `{CALLSIGN}-{YYYYMMDD}.adif`
  - Field Day: `{CALLSIGN}-FD-{YYYYMMDD}.adif`
  - Winter FD: `{CALLSIGN}-WFD-{YYYYMMDD}.adif`
  - `/` in callsigns replaced with `_` (portable calls)

- **Export to `~/Documents/duklog/`**: Files land in a dedicated subdirectory (created automatically) instead of the home root. Falls back to `~/duklog/` if the documents directory is unavailable.

- **Editable export path**: The path on the export screen is a live text field backed by `tui-textarea`. Supports `Left`/`Right`, `Home`/`End`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, and printable characters. `Esc` cancels; `Enter` exports.

- **`park_ref` is now required on POTA logs**: The `DefaultFilename` trait is implemented per log variant; POTA logs always have a park reference.

- **`DefaultFilename` trait**: Each log variant owns its filename format. `default_export_path()` delegates to `log.default_filename()`.

## Breaking change — v0.5.0

POTA logs stored by earlier versions of duklog that are **missing a `park_ref`** in their metadata file cannot be loaded by this version. Attempting to load such a log returns `StorageError::CorruptMetadata`. All logs created with the in-app form were always required to have a park ref; only logs constructed directly or stored by very early builds would be affected.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make ci` passes (693 tests)
- [ ] Create a POTA log with a park ref → export → confirm filename is `{CALL}@{PARK}-{DATE}.adif` in `~/Documents/duklog/`
- [ ] Create General, FD, WFD logs → confirm `-FD-` / `-WFD-` in filenames
- [ ] On export screen: Left/Right move cursor; Home/End jump; Backspace/Delete remove characters; typing inserts at cursor; Enter exports to edited path; Esc returns without exporting

## Summary
- Updated `CChunkFile::Get` to call `memcpy` with explicit C linkage.
- Replaced the C++-linkage declaration with `extern "C"` so the generated call target matches the original object.

## Units/functions improved
- Unit: `main/chunkfile`
- Function: `Get__10CChunkFileFPvl`

## Progress evidence
- `Get__10CChunkFileFPvl`: **99.73684% -> 100.0%**
- `main/chunkfile` `.text`: **99.97537% -> 100.0%**
- No regressions introduced in this unit's code sections.

## Plausibility rationale
- This change is source-plausible: `memcpy` is a standard C library routine and the original build expects C linkage for this call site.
- No compiler-coaxing constructs or non-idiomatic control-flow changes were introduced.

## Technical details
- Remaining mismatch in `Get__10CChunkFileFPvl` was a single call-target relocation at the `bl memcpy` site.
- Making the declaration `extern "C" void* memcpy(void*, const void*, unsigned long);` aligned linkage and resolved the function-level mismatch.

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce onboarding, persistent user preferences and push notifications to improve first-run experience and engagement.
- Extend job data model and map Firestore documents to richer job detail screens for a better UX when source fields are missing.
- Improve navigation, search, bookmarking and category listing to make the app functional with remote Firestore data.
- Add assets, layouts and dependencies needed for Glide, Firebase, navigation and modern UI patterns.

### Description
- Added onboarding flow with `OnboardingActivity`, pager adapter and layouts, and gated app entry using `UserPreferences` to track completion.
- Integrated Firestore job reads across `HomeFragment`, `SearchFragment`, and `CategoryFragment`, added `JobMapper` to safely map `DocumentSnapshot` to the extended `Job` model with fallbacks, and added `firebase/*` docs describing schema and topic usage.
- Implemented push notification handling via `JobFirebaseMessagingService`, requested runtime notification permission in `MainActivity`, and subscribe/unsubscribe to topic `job_alerts` based on `UserPreferences` and `SettingsFragment` toggles.
- Added settings UI in `SettingsFragment` and `UserPreferences` utilities for dark mode, notifications and onboarding flags, and applied theme at startup via `MainActivity.applyThemeFromPreference()`.
- Enhanced navigation and top app bar behavior in `MainActivity`, improved bottom navigation handling and back behavior, and added `OnboardingActivity` start logic when needed.
- Upgraded and added dependencies in `app/build.gradle.kts` including RecyclerView, Navigation, Firebase BOM and Glide, and added numerous UI/layout/resource files and drawable icons for the new screens.
- Implemented bookmarking persistence with `BookmarkManager` using JSON serialization, added save/remove/isSaved helpers, and wired bookmark interactions in `JobAdapter`, `BookmarkFragment` and job detail navigation.
- Improved job list and job detail UI: Glide-based logo loading in `JobAdapter` and `JobDetailFragment`, richer `fragment_job_detail.xml`, swipe-to-refresh in `fragment_home.xml`, search input and results UI in `fragment_search.xml`, and category counts loaded from Firestore in `CategoryFragment`.

### Testing
- Performed a local assemble and sanity build check with `./gradlew assembleDebug`, which completed successfully.
- Ran a static lint/build verification with `./gradlew lint` which returned without blocking errors.
- No new automated unit or instrumented tests were added in this change set.

body:
## Summary

Introduces the **venture-architect** skill, a comprehensive end-to-end workflow that transforms raw startup ideas into complete, investor-ready venture artifacts in a single autonomous execution loop. The skill chains six specialist roles (Research Analyst, Entrepreneur, Product Manager, Systems Architect, Engineering Planner, Deck Creator) to produce a full project scaffold with feasibility analysis, business requirements, product specifications, system architecture, implementation plan, and pitch deck.

## Key Changes

- **Main skill definition** (`SKILL.md`): 330-line specification defining the venture-architect workflow, including:
  - Trigger conditions (user says "this is an idea", "I have a venture idea", etc.)
  - 10-step autonomous process from idea capture through final quality checks
  - No-nudge policy requiring agents to announce actions rather than ask permission
  - Detailed role descriptions for each of the six specialist personas
  - Output structure and quality checklist

- **Six reference templates** for generated documents:
  - `feasibility-report-template.md`: Evidence-based analysis with FACT/INTERPRETATION/ASSUMPTION/UNRESOLVED tags, top 3 showstoppers, and technical spike proposals
  - `brd-template.md`: Market wedge, problem severity, target customer, supply chain resilience, distribution model, unfair advantage, and unit economics
  - `prd-template.md`: Personas, 30-day POC scope, 90-day MVP with MoSCoW prioritization, user stories with acceptance criteria, and success metrics
  - `srs-template.md`: System architecture, major components, interfaces, deployment topology, data flow diagrams, scalability assumptions, and technology choices
  - `implementation-sketch-template.md`: Repository structure, module breakdown, five development phases (Spike → Foundation → MVP → Integration → Deployment), CI/CD pipeline outline
  - `pitch-deck-template.md`: Five-slide executive deck (Problem, Solution, Market Opportunity, Architecture Advantage, Roadmap) with speaker notes and visual suggestions

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Autonomous execution**: Skill runs without user prompts between phases; agents announce progress and only ask for input when private business information or domain clarification is genuinely required
- **Evidence-based analysis**: Feasibility Report uses explicit tagging (FACT/INTERPRETATION/ASSUMPTION/UNRESOLVED) to distinguish evidence levels and confidence
- **Risk-driven design**: Technical Spike Proposals directly address highest-risk assumptions identified in feasibility analysis
- **Structured prioritization**: PRD separates 30-day POC (tied to spike validation) from 90-day MVP with explicit MoSCoW categorization and REQ-NNN IDs
- **Architecture-first SRS**: Requires at least one Mermaid diagram following PDF-safe guidelines (max 15 nodes, <40 char labels)
- **Phase-based implementation**: Five-phase plan (Spike → Foundation → MVP → Integration → Deployment) with explicit dependencies and deliverables
- **Quality gates**: Comprehensive checklist covering all six documents, evidence tagging, persona/story completeness, diagram inclusion, and formatting compliance

The skill integrates with common skills (`agent-todo-ledger`, `design-readiness-gate`, `document-tail-sections`, `output-formatting`, `quality-checklist`, `mermaid-to-pdf`) and is tested against `claude-code` agent.

author: junaiddshaukat
body:
## Summary
Adds support for configuring the Gemini and Vertex AI API base URLs via environment variables, while enforcing safe URL usage. This enables routing CLI traffic through proxies or custom gateways without changing code, and keeps the default behavior unchanged when env vars are not set.
## Details
- **Base URL resolution**
  - For `AuthType.USE_GEMINI` and `AuthType.USE_VERTEX_AI` (and `GATEWAY`), we now resolve a `baseUrl` as:
    - Prefer `config.baseUrl` if provided (e.g., from gateway / higher-level config)
    - Otherwise read from:
      - `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` when not using Vertex AI
      - `GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL` when using Vertex AI
- **Security / validation**
  - Introduces `validateBaseUrl(baseUrl: string)` in `contentGenerator.ts`
  - Ensures the URL is well-formed
  - Requires `https:` for non-local hosts
  - Allows `http:` only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]` to support local development
- **SDK wiring**
  - The resolved, validated `baseUrl` is passed into `GoogleGenAI` via `httpOptions.baseUrl`
  - When no base URL is provided (no config override and no env var), behavior is unchanged

Touched files:
- `packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.ts`
- `packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.test.ts`

## Related Issues

Fixes #6746

## How to Validate

1. **Unit tests (core only)**
   `
   npx vitest run packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.test.ts
`
Expected: all tests pass, including new cases for env-based baseUrl and validateBaseUrl.

**2. Manual sanity check – default behavior**
`npm run build
GEMINI_API_KEY=<your_key> npm start
`

- CLI should behave exactly as before (no custom base URL set).

**3. Manual sanity check – custom Gemini base URL**

`npm run build
GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com \
GEMINI_API_KEY=<your_key> \
npm start`
- CLI should still work normally (explicit base URL matches default endpoint).

**4. Optional: local proxy test**

`# run a local HTTP server on 8080 that logs requests
GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 \
GEMINI_API_KEY=<your_key> \
npm start
`
- Requests should be routed to the local server (HTTP only allowed for localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]).

**5. Negative check: insecure non-local URL**

Set `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=http://evil-proxy.example.com `and start the CLI.
Expected: startup fails with Custom base URL must use HTTPS unless it is localhost.

- [X] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)

## Summary

- Adds `poetry_quality_and_curation/` directory for poem quality workstreams
- Includes tashkeel (diacritization) pipeline as a git submodule pointing to our [Mishkal fork](https://github.com/lesmartiepants/mishkal/tree/fix/tashkeel-bugs)
- Upstream PR submitted: https://github.com/linuxscout/mishkal/pull/74

## What's in the submodule

### Mishkal Bug Fixes (5 commits)
| Fix | Impact |
|-----|--------|
| Increase default word limit 1000 → 20000 | Structural |
| Remove duplicate diacritics + impossible hamza-sukun | 35,928 + 23,745 poems |
| Fix `vocalize_foreign` for unknown words | 23,745 poems |
| Correct spurious shadda on function words (على، إلى) | 19,836 poems |
| Add sun letter assimilation after definite article | 2,226 poems |

### Pipeline (`pipeline/`)
Numbered-step convention matching other curation workstreams:

author: p1ngb4ck
body:
~~1. depends on #17472 now~~ merged. BIG TY bdraco, clyde, swoboda1337 and all others helping me out

Sorry for force-push :( -> rebased on latest version + dependency listed above and re-implemented hopefully clean version now using all latest changes (load_settings) etc.

# What does this implement/fix?

Adds support for WCH CH9344 (4-port) and CH348 (8-port) USB UART bridges via a new `ch9344` and `ch348` type in `usb_uart`.

- Auto-detects CH9344 vs CH348 from the USB device descriptor to determine the correct number of channels
- Each channel is independently configurable (baud rate, data bits, stop bits, parity)

Why two config types (ch9344 / ch348) for the CH934X family instead of one

The CH934X family could have collapsed into a single ch934x type, but we deliberately kept two. The two sub-families are distinguished by USB PID (0xE018 = CH9344, 4 ports; 0x55D9 = CH348, 8 ports) and differ in port count. Keeping them as separate types lets max_channels be validated exactly at config time (4 vs 8), so a config with too many channels is caught during validation rather than only at boot.

A single combined type would have had to advertise the family maximum (8) as its channel ceiling, which would let an 8-channel config validate against a 4-port CH9344 and only fail (or silently load just 4 channels) at runtime. Two types avoid that ambiguity while still keeping the config small.

We did drop the per-chip L/Q variants (CH9344L/Q, CH348L/Q): those share their family's PID and are indistinguishable over USB descriptors, so they never warranted their own type. The driver already resolves the exact sub-variant at boot (PID for the port count, a register bit for L vs Q), so nothing is lost by not exposing them in the config.

body:
#### Reference Issues/PRs

Fixes #745.
#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

This PR implements transparency improvements for the implicit Gaussian fallback logic in the base class of probabilistic regressors, as proposed in #745.
Key changes:
1.Tag Declaration: Added distribution:fallback (defaulting to "Normal") and distribution:fallback_warn (defaulting to True) tags to BaseProbaRegressor.
2._predict_proba Warning: Emits a UserWarning when an estimator does not implement its own _predict_proba
 and defaults to constructing a Normal distribution from predict and predict_var.
3._predict_var Warning: Emits a UserWarning when variance is reconstructed from the Inter-Quartile Range (IQR) under the assumption of Gaussian symmetry (which happens if neither _predict_proba nor _predict_var are overridden).
4.Suppression Support: These warnings can be silenced by setting the "distribution:fallback_warn": False tag, allowing developers of intentional Gaussian estimators to maintain a clean output.

#### Does your contribution introduce a new dependency? If yes, which one?


No


#### What should a reviewer concentrate their feedback on?


1.The wording of the warning messages to ensure they are helpful but not overly intrusive.
2.The logic for identifying fallback paths in  _predict_proba and  _predict_var.
3.Verification that the use of stacklevel=2 correctly points the warning to the user-facing method call (e.g., predict_proba).


#### Did you add any tests for the change?


I have verified the changes locally using a verification script that confirmed:

1. Warnings are emitted when both fallback paths are triggered.
2.Warnings are successfully suppressed via the distribution:fallback_warn tag.
3.Distribution results remain mathematically identical to the previous implementation.


#### Any other comments?

This contribution is part of my GSoC 2026 application for Project 1: "Help implement estimators and compositors from the wishlists.

This pull request introduces support for configurable alert entry storage backends in the Observer component, allowing users to choose between SQLite (default) and PostgreSQL for persisting alert and incident entries. It includes the necessary configuration, validation, dependency injection, and Helm chart changes to support both backends, as well as updates to the codebase to initialize and manage the new storage layers.

**Observer alert/incident storage backend support:**

* Added `alertStoreBackend` and `alertStoreDSN` configuration options to allow choosing between SQLite and PostgreSQL for alert entry storage, with sensible defaults and validation logic in `AlertingConfig` and its loader/validator (`internal/observer/config/config.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-32af72bec430d0d5ec2e02774b58b675aa9a29b8b660762f1f12980fabc315acR111-R115) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-32af72bec430d0d5ec2e02774b58b675aa9a29b8b660762f1f12980fabc315acR198-R199) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-32af72bec430d0d5ec2e02774b58b675aa9a29b8b660762f1f12980fabc315acR349-R350) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-32af72bec430d0d5ec2e02774b58b675aa9a29b8b660762f1f12980fabc315acR428-R442)
* Updated the Observer service initialization to create, initialize, and clean up `alertEntryStore` and `incidentEntryStore` based on configuration, and inject them into the `AlertService` (`cmd/observer/main.go`, `internal/observer/service/alerts.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c396d8ee377761a43fca284545cb4ee535f868ea2b16db01db81a21741855ed8R27-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c396d8ee377761a43fca284545cb4ee535f868ea2b16db01db81a21741855ed8R166-R205) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cb5a8af45777bdb3d6057f1ab9b91534fc6035f1526355072127cbae40c99349L27-R31) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cb5a8af45777bdb3d6057f1ab9b91534fc6035f1526355072127cbae40c99349L52-R60) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-cb5a8af45777bdb3d6057f1ab9b91534fc6035f1526355072127cbae40c99349R72-R73) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-cb5a8af45777bdb3d6057f1ab9b91534fc6035f1526355072127cbae40c99349R83-R84)

**Helm chart and deployment enhancements:**

* Added Helm values and schema for `observer.alertStoreBackend`, `observer.alertStoreSecret`, and `observer.alertStoreSqliteSize`, with logic to provision a PVC for SQLite and require a Secret for PostgreSQL. Added deployment-time validation to prevent misconfiguration (e.g., SQLite with multiple replicas). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bd387735a71f5cea83c08ae06006319e4b0b7a64ca0ca19f6de73c62a2bcb959R1558-R1594) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-94d6c293793c60fc65baa0fcff151f7d1c0b5127349cc1b09a01d232e1d6ffefR893-R924) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ef9cfc98e86f8706f2b2ca4f0fd67c444300ce456e242caeb787fb46fe1b9a2eR1-R17) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f9a62b2edc4ff66205af1531e9988574d7f2f1cd01aabdf96b2383e89301a440R1-R6) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-f9a62b2edc4ff66205af1531e9988574d7f2f1cd01aabdf96b2383e89301a440R78-R86) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-f9a62b2edc4ff66205af1531e9988574d7f2f1cd01aabdf96b2383e89301a440R135-R138) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-f9a62b2edc4ff66205af1531e9988574d7f2f1cd01aabdf96b2383e89301a440R178-R182)

**Dependency updates:**

* Added dependencies for PostgreSQL (`github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` and related) and SQLite (`modernc.org/sqlite` and related) drivers in `go.mod`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R40) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R51-R65) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R74-R76) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6L126-R138)

**Test and codebase adjustments:**

* Updated tests and service constructors to accommodate the new alert/incident store dependencies. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6c644a2080d3162f80141cc41c0908860e164f3fc0fab2550bdc1b1a1f43a733L215-R215) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6c644a2080d3162f80141cc41c0908860e164f3fc0fab2550bdc1b1a1f43a733L586-R586)

These changes make alert and incident entry storage in Observer more flexible and production-ready, supporting both lightweight and scalable backends depending on deployment needs.

## Approach
- Added alert entry store with SQLite and PostgreSQL support
- Updated Helm values schema and values.yaml for alert store configuration
- Implemented persistent volume claim for SQLite storage
- Enhanced alert service to write alert entries to the new store
- Added incident entry store with SQLite and PostgreSQL support
- Enhanced alert service to write incident entries
- Implemented initialization and write operations for incident entries
- Added unit tests for incident entry storage functionality

author: changocircle
body:
## Dog Profile Sync Layer

Bidirectional, local-first sync for dog profiles with conflict resolution favoring most recent `updated_at`.

### How it works

1. **Local-first**: All mutations go to Zustand store instantly. UI never waits for network.
2. **Auto-queue**: Store subscriber detects changes and queues pending sync ops in AsyncStorage.
3. **Smart coalescing**: create+update stays create, create+delete drops entirely, update+update keeps latest.
4. **Push/pull sync**: Pushes pending local changes, fetches remote state, merges with conflict resolution.
5. **Realtime**: Supabase Realtime subscription triggers immediate sync on remote changes.
6. **Foreground sync**: Auto-syncs when app returns to foreground.
7. **Debounced**: Rapid local changes debounce to a single sync after 2 seconds.

### Conflict resolution

When the same dog is modified on two devices:
- Compare `updated_at` timestamps
- Most recent wins, regardless of which device
- Losing side gets overwritten on next sync

### Pre-auth migration

Dogs created before auth (`user_id: "local"`) are automatically migrated to the real user ID on first sign-in and pushed to Supabase.

### New files
- `src/services/dogSync.ts` - Core sync engine (push, pull, merge, realtime, migration)
- `src/hooks/useDogSync.ts` - React hook managing sync lifecycle
- `supabase/migrations/002_dog_sync.sql` - Schema updates + trigger fix + Realtime

### Modified files
- `src/stores/dogStore.ts` - Added `_syncMeta` state + `_mergeDogs` action
- `src/hooks/useDog.ts` - Rewritten as local-first reads (no more TanStack Query for dogs)
- `src/lib/resetStores.ts` - Clears sync data on sign-out
- `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` - Initializes `useDogSync()` hook

### Migration 002 details
- Adds `archived_at`, `gotcha_date`, `onboarding_completed` columns (IF NOT EXISTS)
- Fixes `updated_at` trigger to preserve explicit timestamps from sync clients
- Enables Supabase Realtime on dogs table

### No breaking changes
- All existing dogStore consumers work unchanged
- Sync activates only when user is authenticated
- Without auth, everything stays local-only (same as before)

## Summary
Enhanced the Career Path Explorer input form with richer profile data collection. Users can now upload CVs/resumes, add project/portfolio links, and select skills and interests from predefined categories with custom tag support.

## Key Changes

- **CV/Resume Upload**: Added drag-and-drop file upload zone that accepts text, markdown, CSV, and PDF formats. Text content is extracted (up to 3000 chars) and included in the AI prompt for better context.

- **Skill & Interest Chips**: Replaced simple textarea inputs with categorized chip selectors:
  - Skills: Technical, Data & ML, Engineering & Design, Business & Soft Skills
  - Interests: Science & Technology, Business & Society, Creative & Culture
  - Each category has predefined chips with toggle selection
  - Custom tags can be added via text input for values not in presets

- **Sidebar Width**: Increased from 260px to 340px to accommodate the new form elements.

- **Preset System Update**: Modified preset loading to work with the new chip/tag system instead of textarea values, with proper clearing and reapplication logic.

- **Prompt Enhancement**: Updated `treePrompt()` to include CV content, uploaded filename, and project URLs when available, providing richer context to the AI model.

## Implementation Details

- New CSS classes for upload zones, URL rows, chips, and tag inputs with hover/focus states
- `initChips()` dynamically populates chip groups from `SKILL_CHIPS` and `INTEREST_CHIPS` constants
- Helper functions: `getSkills()`, `getInterests()`, `getChipValues()`, `getTagValues()`, `applyChipsAndTags()`
- CV handling with FileReader API for text extraction; binary files tracked by filename only
- URL management with dynamic row creation/removal via `addUrlRow()` and `getGithubUrls()`
- Tag input supports Enter/comma delimiters and backspace deletion

### Motivation
- Centralize feedback video selection to auto-discovered files in the `MEDIA_VIDEO_FOLDER` instead of relying on manual textarea inputs to avoid invalid paths and duplicates.
- Normalize and validate video paths coming from the media folder to ensure only root-level media files with allowed extensions are used.

- Changed media settings submission to use auto-discovered `autoFeedbackVideos` via `combineVideoLists(autoFeedbackVideos)` and populate `state.feedbackMedia` with a shared list for both `success` and `fail` modes.

## Summary by Sourcery

더 견고한 SSE 처리와 더 명확한 클라이언트 중단(Abort) 의미 체계를 위해 채팅 API 스트리밍과 중단 처리 로직을 개선합니다.

개선 사항:
- 클라이언트가 연결을 닫았을 때 사용할 HTTP 상태 코드 499에 대해 이름이 있는 상수를 도입해, 클라이언트 중단 응답을 문서화하고 표준화합니다.
- TypeScript 타입 내로잉을 활용할 수 있도록 `AbortError` 타입 가드를 강화하여, 더 안전한 에러 처리를 가능하게 합니다.
- 공유 헬퍼를 통해 SSE 라인 파싱과 말단(trailing) 데이터 플러시를 통합하여, 스트림 종료 시점과 일반 읽기 과정 모두에서 일관된 이벤트 처리가 이루어지도록 합니다.
- 사용자가 중단을 요청했을 때 UI 청크 스트림이 조용하고(idempotent) 우아하게 종료되도록 보장하여, 부분 결과는 유지하면서도 불필요한 에러 로그가 발생하지 않도록 합니다.

## Summary by Sourcery

Refine chat API streaming and abort handling for more robust SSE processing and clearer client-abort semantics.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a named constant for the 499 client-closed HTTP status code to document and standardize client abort responses.
- Strengthen the AbortError type guard to leverage TypeScript type narrowing for safer error handling.
- Unify SSE line parsing and trailing data flushing through a shared helper to ensure consistent event processing at stream end and during normal reads.
- Ensure graceful, idempotent completion of the UI chunk stream on user-initiated aborts to avoid noisy error reporting while preserving partial results.

## Summary

Add complete CI/CD pipeline for the anna project.

### Workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Lint and Test** | Push (branches), PRs to main | golangci-lint + `go test -race` with coverage upload |
| **Docker** | Push/PR to main | Build & validate Docker image; push to GHCR on main |
| **Release** | `v*.*.*` tags | GoReleaser binaries + multi-platform Docker with manifest merge |

### Infrastructure

- **Dockerfile** — Multi-stage (golang builder → distroless), runs `anna gateway`
- **.goreleaser.yaml** — Binary releases for linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64
- **.golangci.yml** — golangci-lint v2 config (errcheck, govet, staticcheck, gocritic, misspell)
- **mise.toml** — Added golangci-lint 2.11.1, goreleaser 2.14.1; Go 1.23→1.24; reorganized tasks with release section

### Design decisions

- Lint job uses `continue-on-error: true` — there are ~50 pre-existing `errcheck` issues to fix in a follow-up
- Release Docker tags skip `latest` for prerelease versions (e.g. `v1.2.3-rc.1`)
- Docker manifest merge waits for both GoReleaser and Docker jobs to prevent partial releases
- All workflows use ubicloud runners and mise for tool management, consistent with tokenflux

## Follow-up work

- [ ] Fix ~50 pre-existing `errcheck` lint issues, then remove `continue-on-error` from lint job
- [ ] Add coverage threshold or PR comment reporting

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run lint` runs (reports pre-existing issues, does not block)
- [x] `mise run test` passes
- [x] `mise run release:check` validates goreleaser config
- [x] CI lint-and-test workflow passes (lint soft-fail, test green)
- [x] CI docker workflow passes (build-only on PR)

Users can now pick a ROM file from their local disk instead of pasting a URL.  The host's ROM is stored in browser IndexedDB via PouchDB and replicated to a server-side PouchDB endpoint (express-pouchdb at /api/romdb).  Guest clients automatically pull the ROM from the server when the game-started message arrives, so every player loads the same bytes with no manual URL sharing required.

- public/js/nes-adapter.js: add loadROMBytes(ArrayBuffer) — skips proxy fetch
- public/js/snes-adapter.js: add loadROMBytes(ArrayBuffer) — skips proxy fetch

- public/js/app.js: file-change listener shows size/name feedback; start-game handler stores file via romStore and sends romId; onGameStarted resolves romId to bytes before calling startNESGame/startSNESGame/startLibretroGame; all three game-start functions accept optional romBytes parameter

author: bandepanu
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `/setup-secrets` skill that encrypts project `.env` files using [sops](https://github.com/getsops/sops) + [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age)
- No external secrets service required — age private key lives locally on the VPS; user chooses their own backup strategy (password manager, USB, etc.)
- Ships with two companion scripts (`sops-run.sh`, `env_to_yaml.py`) so Claude doesn't have to generate them from scratch each time
- Integrates cleanly with the existing `/add-s3-storage` skill — encrypted `secrets.yaml` files are safe to back up to S3

## What it solves

Most NanoClaw users on a VPS have plaintext `.env` files sitting in S3 backups, shell history, and at risk of accidental git commits. This skill moves them to encrypted-at-rest `secrets.yaml` files that are decrypted in memory only, on demand, when a service starts.

## Phases covered

1. Install age + sops
2. Generate age keypair
3. Configure sops (`~/.sops.yaml`)
4. Install companion scripts
5. Encrypt each project's `.env`
6. Create `~/sops-run.sh` wrapper
7. Migrate `docker-compose.yml` from `env_file:` to `environment:` pass-through
8. Create `start.sh` per project
9. Test
10. Update backup script (optional, for `/add-s3-storage` users)

## Test plan

- [ ] Run skill on a fresh NanoClaw VPS install
- [ ] Verify `secrets.yaml` is encrypted and `sops-run.sh` decrypts correctly
- [ ] Verify docker-compose containers receive env vars via `./start.sh`
- [ ] Verify `/add-s3-storage` backup script picks up `secrets.yaml` files

author: jordanbmcgowen
body:
Solunar fixes:

- Moon phase was sourced from solunar.org's moonPhase field, which returns 0–100 illumination percentage. getMoonIcon/getMoonPhaseName expected a 0–1 cycle position, so every phase rendered as "Waning Crescent" (any illumination > 0.875 fell through to the else case). Now computed locally via computeMoonPhase() using a verified reference new moon (Jan 11, 2024 11:57 UTC) and the 29.53-day synodic period — accurate, cycle-aware, waxing/waning correct.

- Solunar API date was derived from new Date() using the viewer's local timezone methods (getDate() etc.). Users outside Central Time could send the wrong calendar date — e.g., someone in UTC+1 at 1 AM sees March 8 locally but should send March 7 to the API. Now uses Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone "America/Chicago" to always derive the correct Central Time date.

Offshore bonus removal:

- Removed the "Offshore Bonus" category (+10 pts for E/NE winds) from calcFishingScore(), its breakdown return object, and the renderScoreBreakdown() keys/names list. The app is for onshore fishing only — whether wind is offshore or onshore doesn't change the score the user sees (wind direction still informs the gulf vs. lake location routing in getRecommendation() since offshore winds flatten surf, but that's an internal location decision, not a user-facing score factor).

### Motivation
- The player could be hard to find or disappear when split because code referenced an arbitrary piece (`pieces[0]`) and the camera used a simple centroid that could drift away from the main piece. 
- Bot AI and player controls could target the wrong piece when a cell was split, causing odd movement/targeting behavior. 
- Camera offsets persisted across restarts and the human cell lacked a consistent visual marker to make it easy to spot on small viewports.

### Description
- Added a `getMainPiece(cell)` helper to pick the largest active piece and replaced direct `pieces[0]` references in bot AI and `updatePlayerTarget` so movement and target selection consistently follow the main piece. 
- Reworked `computeCamera` to smooth the camera toward a weighted position that favors the main piece while still factoring in the overall split-piece center. 
- Reset `cam.x`, `cam.y`, and `cam.zoom` in `resetGame` to avoid stale offsets when starting a new run. 
- Improved player visibility by drawing a white outline ring for the human cell and always rendering the `You` label/mass for human cells even when small.

- Served the game locally with `python3 -m http.server 8001` and validated the updated behavior by loading the page in a Playwright mobile-sized viewport, which succeeded and produced a screenshot artifact.

- **C-1**: Isolate printer/reader variables (`*print-base*`, `*print-radix*`, `*read-base*`, `*read-default-float-format*`) in `%eval-forms` to prevent user code from corrupting result serialization
- **M-1**: Enrich `inspect-object` and `pool-status` content text to include elements, entries, slots, and worker details so MCP clients rendering only `content[].text` see complete information
- **M-3**: Bind `*print-circle*` to T in `%eval-forms` result printing to prevent infinite loops on circular structures
- **M-4**: Return parinfer warning from `lisp-edit-form` when auto-repair adds closing delimiters, surfaced in both normal and dry-run responses
- **M-5**: Truncate output before `sanitize-for-json` in `%truncate-output` to avoid O(n) scanning of megabyte-scale strings
- **M-6**: Zero-pad single-digit chapter numbers in `clhs-lookup` section filename generation (e.g., `7` → `07_.htm`)
- **M-7**: Add fast-path in `sanitize-for-json` that returns the original string when no replacement characters are found

### Additional fixes during implementation
- Resolved circular dependency between `inspect.lisp` and `response-builders.lisp` by moving `format-inspect-elements` to `inspect.lisp`
- Fixed `format-inspect-elements` to handle both lists and vectors (inspection functions return lists via `nreverse`)
- Fixed extra closing parens in `lisp-edit-form.lisp` and `inspect.lisp` tool bodies

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `src/repl-core.lisp` | C-1, M-3, M-5 |
| `src/inspect.lisp` | M-1 (format-inspect-elements, circular dep fix) |

author: siddharth-626
body:
This PR addresses a high-priority security risk where Firestore security rules were overly permissive, allowing any authenticated user to modify or delete data in the 'matches' and 'courts' collections.

### 🚨 Severity: HIGH

### 💡 Vulnerability: Over-permissive Firestore rules
The previous rules allowed any authenticated user to:
- Create, update, or delete any match document, regardless of ownership.
- Modify court metadata (name, location, etc.).
- Write to any 'profile' document via a collection group rule.

### 🎯 Impact: 
An attacker could:
- Delete matches they didn't create.
- Falsify scores or players in any match.
- Deface court information.
- Overwrite user profiles globally.

### 🔧 Fix:
- Implemented ownership checks for 'matches' (only host can delete or full-update).
- Restricted participants to only updating 'players' and 'score' fields in matches.
- Restricted 'courts' write access to only allow 'reviews' updates for standard users; all other edits require admin privileges.
- Secured the 'profile' collection group rule by making it admin-only, as specific path rules already handle user-level writes.

### ✅ Verification:
- Manually reviewed 'firestore.rules' to ensure logic correctly implements the principle of least privilege.
- Verified that existing app functionality (score submission, match proposal response, adding reviews) is still supported by the new rules.

author: peacefulprogress25
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent large same-day outflows by adding a withdraw throttle and keep off-chain / non-KLend assets accounted for in vault pricing. 
- Give governance control over fee recipient and the ability to pause deposits or withdrawals. 
- Support non-KLend strategies reported off-chain (reported-value) so vaults can include external allocations without KLend CPI flows. 

### Description
- Extended `VaultState` with throttle and governance fields: `redeemed_in_period`, `period_start_ts`, `fee_recipient`, `deposits_paused`, `withdrawals_paused`, `non_klend_reported_value`, and `offchain_nav`, and added helper methods `compute_total_assets`, `deposits_are_paused`, and `withdrawals_are_paused`.
- Enforced a 24h withdraw throttle in `withdraw` that limits the period redemptions to `MAX_WITHDRAW_THROTTLE_BPS` of the vault treasury (uses `compute_total_assets`); updated `VAULT_STATE_SIZE` and struct paddings to keep size assertions valid.
- Wired governance/config fields into vault config: added `FeeRecipient`, `PauseDeposits`, `PauseWithdrawals`, and `OffchainNav` to `VaultConfigField` and implemented their update checks in `update_vault_config` with the same admin permission model.
- Applied pause checks to user flows: `deposit` now requires `!vault_state.deposits_are_paused()` and `withdraw` requires `!vault_state.withdrawals_are_paused()`.
- Allowed `withdraw_pending_fees` to be executed by either the vault admin or the `fee_recipient` and added corresponding authorization check.
- Added non-KLend strategy support: `StrategyType` enum and `NonKlendStrategyState` account type plus handler `handler_non_klend_strategy.rs` with instructions `init_non_klend_strategy`, `allocate_to_non_klend_strategy`, and `report_non_klend_strategy_value`, and exposed program entrypoints for them in `lib.rs`.
- Updated holdings/AUM logic to include `non_klend_reported_value` and `offchain_nav` via the new `compute_total_assets` so all deposit/withdraw/fee call sites use the extended total assets computation.
- Added constants `NON_KLEND_STRATEGY_SEED`, `NON_KLEND_ESCROW_SEED`, and `MAX_WITHDRAW_THROTTLE_BPS` (default 500 bps = 5%); added README devnet/governance notes describing multisig fee recipient and pause/offchain NAV usage.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo check` for the workspace and compilation succeeded (no type or missing symbol errors after fixes to struct sizes and minor type suffixes).
- Attempted `cargo fmt --all` but it could not run in this environment because `rustfmt` is not installed for the pinned toolchain (error returned by the toolchain).

author: copilot
body:
`PublishMongoSpec` could issue `replSetInitiate` when `hasReplicaConfig` was false (offline probe found no replica config), even if a live PRIMARY/SECONDARY/ARBITER was already healthy — risking disruption during rollouts.

## Changes

- **`shouldInit` guard** — incorporate `hasHealthyReplicaMember(healthByID)` into the init condition so a healthy live member suppresses `replSetInitiate`:
  ```go
  // before
  shouldInit := !specHasReplicaConfig

  // after
  hasHealthyReplica := hasHealthyReplicaMember(healthByID)
  shouldInit := !specHasReplicaConfig && !hasHealthyReplica
  ```

- **Logging** — prepend `"healthy replica member detected"` to `reconfigReasons` when healthy-replica detection is what prevented init, making it clear in logs why reinit was skipped rather than leaving it implicit.

- **`.gitignore`** — add `replctl` Linux binary alongside existing `replctl.exe`.

body:
New Node.js CLI tool that automates the git staging → AI commit message → commit → push workflow using OpenAI.

## Flow
- **Auto-stage**: if no files are staged, runs `git add .` before proceeding
- **AI message generation**: sends `git diff --staged` to `gpt-4o-mini`, returns a [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org)-style message
- **Interactive validation**: user picks *Use / Edit / Abort* via `inquirer` prompt
- **Commit + optional push**: commits with the chosen message, then prompts to push

## Usage
```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
npm install -g autocommit

# inside any git repo:
autocommit
```

## Structure
- `index.js` — CLI entry point (`bin: autocommit`)
- `src/git.js` — thin wrappers around `simple-git` (stage, diff, commit, push)
- `src/ai.js` — OpenAI call, throws if `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset or response is empty
- `__tests__/` — unit tests for both modules with mocked dependencies

author: copilot
body:
macOS builds don't use `COMPL_STATIC=1`, so the output binary is named `7zz` rather than `7zzs`. The script only searched for `7zzs`, causing all macOS builds to fail.

## Changes

- **`build_7zip.sh`**: Add a fallback `find` for `7zz` in subdirectories when `7zzs` is absent; use `head -n 1 | xargs -I{}` for a single portable copy; improve error message to name both searched binaries.

```bash
# Before
find . -type f -name '7zzs' -exec cp -va {} 7zz \;
[ -f 7zz ] || { echo "Error: 7zzs binary not found after build" >&2; exit 1; }

# After
find . -type f -name '7zzs' -exec cp -va {} 7zz \;
[ -f 7zz ] || find . -mindepth 2 -type f -name '7zz' | head -n 1 | xargs -I{} cp -va {} 7zz
[ -f 7zz ] || { echo "Error: 7zzs or 7zz binary not found after build" >&2; exit 1; }
```

`-mindepth 2` prevents the fallback `find` from matching the `./7zz` destination itself.

author: jin-li
body:
In the markdown, if an external image is referred like following:
```markdown
![An inaccessible image](https://image.com/an_inaccessible_image.png)
```
and the remote image is inaccessible (remote image is broken, or just due to network issue) during the Hugo building process, the build will fail with following message:
```bash
ERROR Unable to get remote resource "https://image.com/an_inaccessible_image.png"
Built in 1849 ms
ERROR error building site: logged 1 error(s)
```

This happens even when the remote itself is fine, but it's just not accessible or loading very slowly during running `hugo server` or `hugo -D` to build the site. 

So I propose that, in `layouts/_partials/helper/image.html`, show warning instead error for inaccessible remote images and so that the Hugo build can continue without broken. 
- If it's just network issue, the images will be loaded later
- If he remote image is broken, user can fix the inaccessible image based on the warning message

author: hardonian
body:
## Description

This PR introduces the **Settler Platform Integration Layer** — a comprehensive subsystem that unifies core reconciliation engine capabilities into a cohesive, deterministic platform.

### Key Additions

**Core Primitives** (`platform/primitives.ts`)
- Canonical types shared across all subsystems: `Execution`, `Artifact`, `Workflow`, `Policy`, `Connector`, `PlatformEvent`, `Proof`, `Tenant`, `AISuggestion`, `ChaosFault`, and `TrustNode`/`TrustEdge`
- Ensures type consistency across trust graph, replay lab, policy simulator, AI copilot, and event backbone

**Trust Graph** (`platform/trust-graph.ts`)
- Content-addressed artifact lineage tracking with deterministic snapshot hashing
- Execution provenance and policy governance relationships
- Tenant isolation enforcement on edges
- Lineage tracing for full execution ancestry/descendancy
- Supports recording executions, artifacts, proofs, and policy governance

**Determinism Enforcement** (`platform/determinism.ts`)
- `DeterminismAuditor`: Detects violations (timestamps, random IDs, AI mutations, connector non-determinism, replay mismatches)
- `DeterministicExecutionFence`: Guards against operations during deterministic execution paths
- `normalizeConnectorOutput()`: Deterministically replaces UUIDs to ensure replay consistency
- `deterministicId()`: Seeded ID generation for stable identifiers

**AI Copilot Safety** (`platform/ai-copilot.ts`)
- AI operates strictly as advisory/analysis — never directly executes workflows or modifies state
- Suggestion creation with audit trails and human review enforcement
- Execution fence prevents AI operations during deterministic runs
- Configurable suggestion limits per execution and allowed categories
- Full acceptance/rejection tracking with policy validation

**Policy Simulator** (`platform/policy-simulator.ts`)
- "What-if" analysis for policy changes against historical executions
- Budget constraint validation (compute, memory, CAS I/O, replay calls)
- Identity constraint checking (roles, scopes)
- Retroactive impact analysis showing how many past executions would be affected
- Policy comparison to evaluate differences

**Chaos Harness** (`platform/chaos-harness.ts`)
- Controlled fault injection into platform subsystems
- Invariant checking for replay correctness, proof integrity, execution idempotency, and tenant isolation
- Scenario-based testing with fault handlers and invariant checkers
- Determinism auditor integration

**Event Consumers** (`platform/event-consumers.ts`)
- `TrustGraphConsumer`: Processes execution/proof/policy events into trust graph
- `ObservabilityConsumer`: Collects all events for tracing and metrics
- `PolicyAuditConsumer`: Tracks policy evaluation decisions
- `ConnectorMetricsConsumer`: Records connector sync performance
- `EventConsumerRegistry`: Manages consumer lifecycle and offset tracking

**Connector Registry** (`platform/connector-registry.ts`)
- Central capability registry enforcing deterministic guarantees
- Output normalization, execution timeouts, sandbox isolation, and retry policies
- Minimum safety requirements validation

**MCP Server Extensions** (`packages/cli/src/mcp/server.ts`)
- New tools: `runWorkflow`, `replayExecution`, `verifyProof`, `inspectPolicy`, `traceArtifact`, `listConnectors`, `eventBackboneHealth`
- Async tool handling with proper error propagation
- Full integration with platform subsystems

### Testing

- **Integration tests** (`platform/__tests__/platform-integration.test.ts`): 696 lines covering all subsystems working together
  - Trust graph node/edge recording, tenant isolation, deterministic snapshots, lineage tracing
  - Determinism auditor violation detection and reporting
  - AI copilot suggestion creation, human review enforcement, execution fence blocking
  - Policy simulator evaluation, comparison, and retroactive impact analysis
  - Chaos harness fault injection and invariant checking
  - Event consumer dispatch and registry management

- **Performance benchmarks** (`platform/__tests__/platform-benchmark.test.ts`): Validates production-scale scenarios
  - Trust graph: 10

author: jdx
body:
## Summary

- Adds `cmd_read_async()` helper in `src/cmd.rs` — wraps `tokio::process::Command` with `kill_on_drop(true)` as an async alternative to `cmd!().read()` (duct)
- Migrates npm and go backend version-fetching paths from blocking `cmd!().read()` to `cmd_read_async()`

## Problem

Inside `run_with_timeout_async` blocks, `cmd!().read()` (duct) is a **synchronous blocking call** — it blocks the tokio worker thread with no yield points. This means:

1. **Timeouts can't fire** — `tokio::time::timeout` works by cancelling futures at `.await` points, but there are none during a blocking `read()` call
2. **Orphaned processes** — `std::process::Child::drop()` does not send a signal, so when a future is dropped, the subprocess continues running as an orphan

## Fix

`cmd_read_async()` uses `tokio::process::Command` which:

- `.output().await` is a real async operation — the timeout can cancel it at the yield point
- `.kill_on_drop(true)` sends SIGKILL to the child when the future is dropped — no orphans

## Scope

This PR migrates the 3 call sites inside async timeout wrappers:
- `src/backend/npm.rs` — `_list_remote_versions()` and `latest_stable_version()`
- `src/backend/go.rs` — `_list_remote_versions()`

The sync `run_fetch_task_with_timeout` callers (ruby, erlang, python, core/go) have the same underlying issue but use a different pattern — they can be addressed in a follow-up.

See #8499 for the full root cause analysis.

## Test plan

- [ ] `mise ls-remote npm:prettier` still works (npm version fetching)
- [ ] `mise ls-remote go:github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/cmd/golangci-lint` still works (go version fetching)
- [ ] Version fetches that exceed `fetch_remote_versions_timeout` now actually time out instead of hanging

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches subprocess execution and environment handling in remote version fetching; behavior changes around cancellation, error reporting, and env clearing could impact some platforms/registries.
> 
> **Overview**
> Version-fetching for the Go and NPM backends is switched from blocking `duct` reads to a new async `cmd_read_async()` helper, so `run_with_timeout_async` can actually cancel long-running `go list`/`npm view` calls.
> 
> `cmd_read_async()` runs subprocesses via `tokio::process::Command` with `kill_on_drop(true)`, and NPM version queries now set `NPM_CONFIG_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=false` via the provided env map while using this async path.

body: ## Changes - **Skip redundant props storage read in `onStart`**: When props are passed directly, `updateProps()` already writes to storage and sets `this.props`. author: sheepdestroyer
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The application's CacheableWebView enabled universal file access and AdBlockWebViewClient intercepted `file://` URIs without validating the canonical path. This allowed potential attackers to read arbitrary files from the file system using a directory traversal payload.
🎯 Impact: Complete Local File Inclusion (LFI). Attackers could read sensitive user data or internal app configurations by manipulating the cached resource URL string.
🔧 Fix:
1. Disabled universal file access on CacheableWebView.
2. Intercept `file://` URLs manually in AdBlockWebViewClient.
3. Verify that the requested file resolves to a canonical path firmly inside the expected application cache directory (e.g. `getCanonicalPath().startsWith(cacheDir)` with a trailing `File.separator`).
✅ Verification: Added tests verifying that directory traversal is blocked and valid cache access remains allowed. Run `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests "io.github.sheepdestroyer.materialisheep.widget.AdBlockWebViewClientTest"`.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [7450452780042854514](https://jules.google.com/task/7450452780042854514) started by @sheepdestroyer*

## Summary by Sourcery

Harden WebView caching against path traversal via file:// URLs and restrict file access in the cacheable WebView.

Bug Fixes:
- Block directory traversal in AdBlockWebViewClient by validating that intercepted file:// requests resolve to canonical paths within the app cache and match expected cache file naming.
- Disable general file access in CacheableWebView to prevent unintended local file reads from WebView content.

Enhancements:
- Expose cache file prefix and extension constants so they can be reused for validation when serving cached content.
- Document the resolved path traversal vulnerability and its prevention steps in the Sentinel security notes.

Documentation:
- Add a Sentinel security note describing the path traversal vulnerability in file:// handling, mitigations, and best practices for WebView URL access control.

Tests:
- Add Robolectric tests to verify that traversal attempts via file:// are blocked while legitimate cached resources in the cache directory are still served.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!
