author: s0up4200
body:
## Summary
- When an OIDC provider returns a token without `expires_in` (or with an already-past expiry), `token.Expiry` is the Go zero time, making `time.Until()` return a large negative duration
- This caused sessions to be stored with an already-expired TTL and cookies with a negative max-age, resulting in an infinite redirect loop on `/login` after successful authentication with the OIDC provider
- Falls back to a 24h TTL when the computed session TTL is non-positive

## Details
The OIDC callback handler used `time.Until(token.Expiry)` in three places:
1. Cache TTL for the session
2. `ExpiresAt` field in `SessionData`
3. Cookie `max-age`

If the provider omits `expires_in` from the token response, the `oauth2` library leaves `Token.Expiry` as the zero value (`0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`). `time.Until(zeroTime)` produces a massive negative duration, causing:
- The cache item to be stored with an already-past expiration (immediately treated as expired on `Get()`)
- The cookie to have a negative max-age (browser may discard it)

Observed with Authentik as the OIDC provider — after successful authentication, the frontend's `/api/auth/oidc/verify` call would find no session, triggering a redirect loop.

getCurrentRound() previously only checked completed round data (rounds[i] !== null). At the start of R3, golfers mid-round still have rounds[2]=null, so it returned 1 (R2) even though R3 had started — causing cut penalty scores to not be applied.

Now also checks if any active golfer has a numeric thru value (meaning they've teed off), and infers the in-progress round from their completed round count. This fires as soon as the first golfer tees off in R3 or R4.

author: davebarnwell
body:
## Summary

This change adds first-class Rollbar user querying to the CLI so agents and operators can look up account users directly from the terminal before assigning items. Before this change the CLI supported items and occurrences, but there was no way to resolve valid assignee IDs without leaving the tool or calling the Rollbar API manually.

The user-facing effect was friction in incident triage workflows: item assignment commands accepted user IDs, but the CLI could not help discover those IDs. That made assignment workflows slower and made the shipped skill documentation incomplete for agent-driven triage.

The root cause was that the client, command, and UI layers only implemented item and occurrence endpoints. There was no normalized user model, no `users` command group, and no documentation/examples for account-user lookup.

This PR adds `users list` and `users get` commands, including text output plus the structured output modes used elsewhere in the CLI (`json`, `raw-json`, and `ndjson`). It adds the Rollbar client support for `/api/1/users` and `/api/1/user/{id}`, renders both list and single-user text views, and updates the README and Rollbar skill examples so assignment workflows can reference the new commands directly.

## Validation

I validated the change with the existing Go test suite after implementation:

- `go test ./...`

author: copilot
body:
The app was still encoding product semantics in generic UI helpers and treating document/canvas as separate content systems. This change moves category presentation into persisted metadata and establishes a shared serialized page structure that both renderers can project.

- **Category metadata is now the source of truth**
  - Added persisted `category.metadata.icon` instead of deriving icons from category ids.
  - Kept seeded categories as data only; UI no longer special-cases `worlds`, `locations`, `factions`, `characters`, `lore`, or `bestiary`.
  - Added migration-safe normalization so existing stored categories load with appropriate metadata.

- **Generic icon rendering**
  - Removed hardcoded built-in category icon lookup from `src/lib/icons.ts`.
  - Replaced it with a generic icon-name registry (`book-open`, `folder`, `globe`, etc.).
  - Updated `Sidebar` to render `category.metadata.icon` directly.

- **Shared page/block/entity/relation structure**
  - Added a canonical serialized model in `src/lib/document-pages.ts`:
    - `PageRecord`
    - `BlockRecord`
    - `EntityRecord`
    - `RelationRecord`
    - `PageContentModel`
  - Persisted that shared model alongside page content in `src/lib/document.ts`.
  - Synced page metadata, category membership, and ordering into the shared page model during load/create/update paths.

- **Document/canvas architecture clarified**
  - Updated page-mode descriptions and editor boundary docs to describe document and canvas as projections over shared page state, not disconnected modes.
  - Document-mode draggable blocks remain an editor affordance over meaningful block units; they do not define the canonical schema.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated the README to describe the shared page structure and the shift from seeded category assumptions to persisted category metadata.

Example of the new category-driven icon flow:

```ts
export interface CategoryMetadata {
  icon: CategoryIconName;
}

export interface Category {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  newLabel: string;
  docIds: string[];
  metadata: CategoryMetadata;
}

// UI reads category metadata directly
const CategoryIcon = getCategoryIcon(category.metadata.icon);
```

- **Screenshot**
  - New arbitrary category rendering without built-in id assumptions:  
    ![Sidebar category metadata screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e7fdc81-fbf9-4cb4-9c96-8fef1ca284c6)

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


----

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>Unify document/canvas structure and remove entity-specific UI assumptions</issue_title>
<issue_description># Unify document/canvas structure and remove entity-specific UI assumptions

## Problem

The current app still mixes domain-specific assumptions into generic UI and data-model layers.

Examples:

- Category icon selection is hardcoded in UI code in `src/lib/icons.ts` through `BUILTIN_CATEGORY_ICONS`.
- Category structure is partially generic in storage, but presentation behavior still assumes fixed worldbuilding entities like worlds, locations, factions, characters, lore, and bestiary.
- The Lexical editor and canvas are still treated as separate content systems rather than two views over a shared page/block/entity model.

This makes the UI less flexible, makes schema evolution harder, and pushes product semantics into rendering utilities that should stay generic.

## Goal

Create a single flexible structure that supports both Lexical document editing and canvas views, while removing entity-specific UI logic from the generic shell.

## Required direction

### 1. Remove entity-specific UI references

- Remove hardcoded category icon mappings like `BUILTIN_CATEGORY_ICONS` from `src/lib/icons.ts`.
- Do not encode category meaning in UI utility code via constants or switch/lookup tables tied to specific category ids.
- Move icon selection into category metadata so categories define their own icon values dynamically.
- Keep the UI shell generic: it should render category metadata, not infer semantics from ids like `worlds`, `locations`, `factions`, `characters`, `lore`, or `bestiary`.

### 2. Make category metadata explicit and flexible

- Extend category metadata so icon, and any future presentation metadata, live with the category record itself.
- Ensure persisted category metadata remains serializable and migration-safe.
- Treat built-in/default categories as seeded data only, not as special-case UI behavior.

### 3. Unify Lexical and canvas around a shared structure

- Define a shared page/content model instead of treating document mode and canvas mode as unrelated content systems.
- The structure should distinguish:
  - page metadata
  - block/content structure
  - entity records
  - relations/references
- Lexical should be one renderer/editor over that structure.
- Canvas should be another renderer/editor over the same underlying concepts, not a disconnected mode.

### 4. Follow Lexical node best practices

Use current Lexical guidance when introducing app-specific structure:

- Prefer built-in nodes where possible.
- Use custom nodes only where there is real app-specific semantic value.
- Use `$config` and `NodeState` for custom node metadata rather than ad hoc serialized properties where practical.
- Keep custom node constructors compatible with collaboration requirements, including zero-required-argument construction.
- Keep document-level metadata out of `RootNode`.

### 5. Keep draggable blocks as document-mode affordance, not the data model

- Keep/finish the draggable block editor UX in Lexical.
- Ensure drag-and-drop reorders meaningful block units.
- Do not let the draggable-block UI define the canonical app schema.

## Suggested implementation shape

Start with a shared content model like:

- `Page`
  - id
  - title
  - mode
  - category membership / ordering metadata
- `Block`
  - block id
  - block type
  - props / node state
  - child block references
- `Entity`
  - entity id
  - entity type
  - domain metadata
- `Relation`
  - source id
  - target id
  - relation type

Then:

- Render/edit block structure in Lexical.
- Render spatial projections of blocks/entities/relations in canvas.
- Use stable ids so document blocks and canvas objects can refer to the same underlying objects.

## Acceptance criteria

- No hardcoded entity/category-specific UI lookups remain in generic rendering helpers.
- Category icons are read from persisted category metadata.
- Default categories can still be seeded, but the UI behaves correctly for arbitrary categories.
- The document/canvas architecture is documented as a shared structure rather than two disconnected content systems.
- Any new custom Lexical nodes follow the current node guidance (`$config`, `NodeState`, collaboration-safe construction).
- Draggable blocks remain enabled for document editing and operate on meaningful block units.

## Recommended order

1. Refactor category metadata first.
  - Move icon and related presentation metadata into persisted category records.
  - Remove UI-level hardcoded category semantics from `src/lib/icons.ts` and related helpers.

2. Define the shared page/block/entity/relation schema next.
  - Do this before introducing more custom Lexical nodes or deeper canvas projection logic.
  - The schema should be the source of truth for how both document mode and canvas mode relate to the same content.

3. Only then add or refine app-sp...

author: madmax983
body:
⚡ Bolt: Replace `.min_by` with `.fold` on DashMap iteration

* 💡 What: Replaced `.iter().min_by(...)` with `.fold(None, ...)` when finding the default vector property name in `CurrentStorage`.
* 🎯 Why: Using `.min_by` on a `DashMap` iterator holds the `RefMulti` read guard of the "current minimum" element across loop iterations. This blocks concurrent writers to that shard for the duration of the entire O(N) iteration, causing heavy lock contention and potential deadlocks.
* 📊 Impact: Significantly reduces lock contention duration on `DashMap` shards from O(N) to O(1) per element, preventing deadlocks and improving concurrent write throughput.
* 🔬 Measurement: Run `cargo bench` or concurrent read/write tests on `enable_vector_index` and `get_default_vector_property_name`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes a deadlock where checkpoint quiescence hangs forever (`paused=0/N`) when the fingerprint store auto-switches to hybrid mode:

- Workers blocked on RwLock during FP store switch couldn't reach their pause point
- Root cause: FP store switch takes write lock, workers wait for read lock, checkpoint waits for workers to pause, but they can't pause while waiting
- Solution: Add `switch_pending` flag that workers check BEFORE acquiring read lock. When switch is pending, workers yield instead of blocking

## Changes

- **src/storage/auto_switching_fingerprint_store.rs**: Add `switch_pending` coordination flag
- **src/storage/unified_fingerprint_store.rs**: Add `is_switch_pending()` method
- **src/chaos.rs**: Add new failpoints and `QuiescenceResult` enum for testing

## Tests

- **spec/CheckpointQuiescence.tla**: TLA+ specification modeling the deadlock scenario (459 lines)
- **tests/checkpoint_properties.rs**: Property-based tests for pause/resume coordination (888 lines)
- **tests/checkpoint_chaos.rs**: Chaos/fault injection tests for edge cases (1080 lines)
- **fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_checkpoint_quiescence.rs**: Fuzzing targets for concurrent operations (636 lines)

author: emeeks
body:
- Root cause: DataSourceAdapter.setBoundedData() dedup cache (if (data === this.lastBoundedData) return) blocked re-ingestion on StrictMode remount because
  React passes the same array reference
- Why previous fixes failed: terser with unsafe: true and pure_getters: true strips every form of useEffect cleanup that only does property writes or
  optional-chain method calls. It also re-inserts dedup guards when it proves a function is idempotent. Over multiple attempts (clearLastData method, direct
  property assignment, removing the dedup, null-then-reassign), terser's two-pass optimization defeated all of them
- Fix that works: setBoundedData([...data]) — spread creates a new array reference on every call, so the === check always passes. The dedup cache stays
  functional for progressive chunking. Shallow copy cost is negligible
- Applied to: StreamXYFrame and StreamOrdinalFrame

-  regression added to dependencies — was used in trend/forecast annotations but never declared, causing Vite resolution failures

author: copilot
body:
Adds a `prompt-library.yaml` config file mechanism to control which prompts are loaded from built-in and runtime sources, using glob-style include/exclude patterns matched against prompt IDs and categories.

## Core: `PromptLibraryFilter`

New data class in `promptkt-core` with four pattern lists:

```yaml
# config/prompt-library.yaml
includeIds: []               # glob patterns on bare prompt ID (e.g. "text-summarize/*")
includeCategories: [ text ]  # glob patterns on category
excludeIds: []
excludeCategories: [ examples ]
```

- If both include lists are empty, all prompts pass the include check
- Excludes are applied after includes
- Patterns are case-insensitive; `*` matches any sequence, `?` matches one character
- Compiled `Regex` objects are cached lazily per filter instance

## Config file loading

Follows the existing `ModelIndex` runtime-override pattern:
1. Explicit path (via `loadFromFileOrDefault(path)`)
2. `prompt-library.yaml` in working directory
3. `config/prompt-library.yaml`
4. Built-in default resource (`tri/ai/prompt/prompt-library.yaml`) — all lists empty (accept-all)

## Integration

- `PromptLibrary.loadDefaultPromptLibrary()` and `loadRuntimePromptLibrary()` apply the filter after loading all prompts
- `PromptGroupIO.readFromDirectory()` and JAR resource loading now skip non-`PromptGroup` YAML files gracefully (fine-level log) instead of propagating parse errors

## Config templates

`prompt-library.yaml` added to `distribution/src/main/dist/config/` and `promptfx/promptfx/config/` with inline documentation.

author: bortlesboat
body:
## Summary
- Sortino ratio used `std()` of only negative excess returns, which overstates downside risk
- Replaced with target downside deviation: `sqrt(mean(min(excess, 0)^2))` across all periods
- This matches the standard definition (Sortino & van der Meer, 1991) and is consistent with libraries like `ffn` and `empyrical`

## Why this matters
The old formula has two errors:
1. **Selection bias** — filtering to only negative returns excludes periods where the portfolio met or exceeded the target, inflating the denominator
2. **Bessel's correction** — `Series.std()` uses `ddof=1`, further distorting the result for small samples

In practice this can understate Sortino by ~20% depending on the return distribution.

## Test plan
- [x] All 3 existing metrics tests pass
- [x] Verified numerically: old vs new formula with sample data shows expected ~20% correction

## Summary
`_convert_to_png()` renames the original file to `.bmp` before calling ImageMagick `convert`, then unconditionally deletes the `.bmp` regardless of whether conversion succeeded. **After:** Original file restored on any conversion failure

- Only delete `.bmp` temp file after confirmed successful conversion
- Restore original on convert failure, missing binary, or timeout
- Add 3 tests: failure, not-installed, and timeout scenarios (all verify file preservation)

body:
### Motivation
- Replace the previous server-authoritative schema and hit/knockback logic with a peer-to-peer oriented data model to support peer-declared combat events and reproducible DB resets via a single DDL file.
- Simplify and normalize profile, stats, inventory, position, weapons, skills, quests, and combat event tables to better match a P2P authority model and client expectations.
- Clean up HTTP handler flow, CORS/OPTIONS handling, static file serving, and CLI entrypoint to make the service easier to run and integrate with the lightweight browser client.

### Description
- Added `backend/sql/p2p_schema.sql` and switched `DB._init_schema` to load the canonical schema from `SCHEMA_PATH` on startup, dropping legacy tables and creating new normalized tables such as `game_profiles`, `stats`, `positions`, `weapons`, `skills`, `assets`, `inventory`, `quest_progress`, and `combat_events`.
- Reworked `DB` methods and data shapes: replaced `player_profiles` with `game_profiles` and `profile_id`/`profile` naming, changed `weapons` and `skills` columns (e.g. `base_damage`, `fire_rate`, `cooldown_seconds`), updated seed data inserts, and adapted CRUD APIs (`create_user`, `create_profile`, `get_profile`, `list_*`, `set_profile_position`, `set_profile_weapon`, `accept_quest`, `register_hit`) to the new schema and P2P semantics.
- Removed server-side distance/knockback calculations and replaced server hit logging with peer-declared `combat_events` (API responses include `authoritative: "peer"`), and updated stats increments on combat events.

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes several small bugs and typos:

- **Fix error logging**: `e.messages` → `e.message` in the catch handler (`index.ts:24`). The `messages` property doesn't exist on Error objects, so the error message was always logged as `undefined`.

- **Fix memory retrieval logic**: The `getFromMemory` tool previously only returned an error when `vectorQuery.matches` was empty. If matches existed but all had scores below the 0.65 threshold, the `ids` array would be empty, causing `whereIn("id", [])` to produce invalid SQL. Now it checks `ids.length === 0` after filtering, which correctly handles both cases.

- **Fix typos in system prompt**: "AI Assistance" → "AI Assistant", "tasks their ask you to" → "tasks they ask you to"

- **Remove unnecessary escape sequences**: `\'` in template literals doesn't need escaping — removed the backslashes.

## Why this is beneficial

- Error logs now actually contain the error message, making debugging possible
- Memory retrieval no longer produces invalid SQL when vector matches are below threshold
- System prompt is grammatically correct, improving LLM instruction quality

author: jhd3197
body:
Cacao was already good at building UIs fast — now it's better at surviving the real world. This PR adds the production-readiness layer: security primitives, observability tooling, session state that outlives server restarts, and a project scaffolding option for apps that outgrow a single file.

### Highlights

- CSRF protection, input sanitization, OAuth2/OIDC, and role-based access control are available out of the box via `c.enable_csrf()`, `c.sanitize()`, `c.oauth2()`, and RBAC middleware
- Session state persists across server restarts — clients reconnect and pick up where they left off
- Structured logging, Prometheus metrics, distributed tracing, and signal rate monitoring can each be enabled with a single call
- Background task queue for long-running operations that won't block the WebSocket event loop
- `cacao create my-app -t structured` scaffolds a multi-file project with pages, components, handlers, and data directories
- WebSocket reconnection uses exponential backoff with jitter instead of fixed-interval retry
- VirtualList gains stable keys, jump-to-index, scroll throttling, and infinite scroll via `onEndReached`

<details>
<summary>Technical changes</summary>

- New `cacao/server/security.py` (1200 lines): `CSRFProtection` with per-session HMAC tokens, `Sanitizer` for HTML/SQL/path-traversal scrubbing, `OAuth2Provider` with Google/GitHub/custom OIDC flows, `RBAC` with role hierarchy and `require_role` decorator, `AuditLogger` with `audit_middleware`
- New `cacao/server/observability.py` (614 lines): `StructuredLogFormatter` emitting JSON with correlation IDs, `PrometheusMetrics` with counter/gauge/histogram primitives and `/metrics` endpoint, `Tracer` wrapping OpenTelemetry (or lightweight fallback), `SignalRateMonitor` for detecting hot signals
- New `cacao/server/session_persist.py`: `SessionStore` saves per-session signal state as JSON files; state restored on reconnect when client sends previous `session_id` query param
- New `cacao/server/tasks.py`: `BackgroundTaskQueue` with semaphore-bounded concurrency, task tracking (`TaskInfo`/`TaskStatus`), cancellation, and graceful shutdown with drain timeout
- `cacao/server/server.py`: Added `GZipMiddleware`, `CachedStaticFiles` with immutable cache headers for fingerprinted assets, asset manifest loading, correlation ID injection per session, metrics/tracing hooks on connect/event/disconnect, CSRF token delivery on session start, permessage-deflate WebSocket compression negotiation
- `cacao/server/app.py`: `startup()` initializes `BackgroundTaskQueue` and records server start time; `shutdown()` saves all session state, broadcasts `server:shutdown`, and drains the task queue
- `cacao/simple.py`: Added 385 lines of simple-API wrappers for all new modules — `enable_session_persistence()`, `background_task()`, `enable_structured_logging()`, `enable_metrics()`, `enable_tracing()`, `enable_signal_monitoring()`, `enable_csrf()`, `sanitize()`, `oauth2()`, RBAC helpers
- `cacao/frontend/build.js`: Asset fingerprinting via MD5 content hashes, generates `manifest.json` mapping original to hashed filenames
- `cacao/frontend/src/components/core/websocket.js`: Configurable reconnection with exponential backoff and jitter (`window.__CACAO_RECONNECT__`), session ID sent on reconnect for state restoration, `batch` message type for grouped signal updates, `server:shutdown` and `ws:reconnected` events
- `cacao/frontend/src/components/display/VirtualList.js`: Stable keys via `id`/`key`/`_id` fields, `jump_to` prop, `requestAnimationFrame`-throttled scroll handler, `end_reached_threshold` for infinite scroll callbacks
- `cacao/cli/commands.py`: New `structured` template option in `cacao create`, `_get_template()` returns `dict[str, str]` for multi-file templates, `_get_structured_template()` generates pages/components/handlers/data skeleton
- New `docs/STRUCTURE.md`: Documents the recommended multi-file project layout
- Rewrote all examples (`counter/`, `todo/`, `dashboard/`, `analytics_dashboard/`) to use the Cacao Python API instead of raw server/TSX patterns; removed obsolete `server.py` and `App.tsx` files
- `cacao/server/__init__.py` and `__all__`: Exports for all new security, observability, session persistence, and task modules

</details>

body:
When a new item is inserted into an entity array, `diffEntityArray` called `diff(undefined, newItem, ...)` which generated a `set` patch — redundant since the splice patch from `computeEntityArrayPatches` already contains the complete data for the inserted item.

The fix skips the diff call for items whose entity key doesn't exist in the old array, as they are fully handled by the splice patch. Existing items that were retained or reordered still get diffed for field-level changes.

author: dylanvdmerwe
body:
This PR fixes two PostgreSQL issues that surfaced while checking for cross-engine regressions after the SQL Server work.

First, the generic parser was incorrectly treating NOW() as a bit literal in default expressions, which broke PostgreSQL defaults like DEFAULT now(). Second, the PostgreSQL pgquery fallback path did not convert CREATE POLICY statements into the generic AST, so policy expressions using casts like current_schema()::uuid failed whenever the generic parser could not handle them directly.

 What changed

  - Fixed the generic parser in parser/parser.y so NOW() is parsed as a function expression instead of a bit literal.
  - Regenerated parser/parser.go.
  - Added PostgreSQL fallback support for CREATE POLICY in database/postgres/parser.go.
  - Added PostgreSQL regression coverage for policy parsing in database/postgres/tests.yml.
  - Added a focused generic parser regression test for DEFAULT now() in parser/parser_test.go.
  - Updated a stale psqldef integration expectation in cmd/psqldef/psqldef_test.go to match the current schema-dependent behavior of skipped unmanaged-function drops.

  Bugs fixed

  - CREATE POLICY ... USING (current_schema()::uuid = current_database()::uuid) now parses through the PostgreSQL fallback path.
  - DEFAULT now() on PostgreSQL timestamp columns no longer normalizes to an invalid bit literal form.

  Testing

  Verified with:

  - go test ./parser -run TestNowFunctionInDefaultExpression -count=1
  - go test ./database/postgres -run TestParse -count=1
  - go test ./cmd/psqldef -count=1 against PostgreSQL 18
  - go test ./cmd/sqlite3def -count=1

  I also reran SQL Server checks after these changes to confirm the MSSQL branch behavior was unaffected:

  - go test ./database/mssql -count=1
  - go test ./cmd/mssqldef -count=1

  Notes

  - This is intentionally separate from the SQL Server parser PR.
  - The NOW() fix lives in the generic parser, but the motivating failure and the added coverage are PostgreSQL-specific.

body:
…e socios

Se agregan tres nuevos endpoints para gestionar el ciclo completo de pagos y renovaciones de membresias:

- GET /api/socios/:id/historial-pagos: Endpoint para consultar el historial completo de membresias y pagos asociados a un socio especifico. Retorna informacion detallada incluyendo plan, fechas, estados de vigencia y pago, precio cobrado, usuario asignador y detalles de cada pago recibido con metodo de pago y cobrador.

- POST /api/socios/:id/pagar-membresia: Endpoint para registrar pagos de membresias atrasadas. Implementa logica inteligente que permite especificar un ID de membresia particular o buscar automaticamente la deuda mas reciente. Valida estado de caja abierta, crea recibo de pago, registra movimiento de ingreso en caja y actualiza estado de membresia a pagado. Incluye manejo de errores especificos para caja cerrada, membresia no encontrada y membresia ya pagada.

- POST /api/socios/:id/renovar: Endpoint para crear un nuevo ciclo de membresia. Calcula automaticamente fechas de inicio y fin basadas en duracion del plan, aplica descuentos de ofertas activas si corresponde, registra el pago inmediato, genera movimiento de ingreso en caja y crea el nuevo registro de membresia en estado activo y pagado. Valida existencia de socio, plan y estado de caja antes de procesar la transaccion.

Implementacion tecnica:
- Todas las operaciones de escritura se ejecutan dentro de transacciones de Prisma para garantizar consistencia de datos
- Se utiliza validacion de metodos de pago mediante funcion helper validarMetodoPago
- Los movimientos de caja se registran con referencias tipo membresia y conceptos de ingreso especificos
- Se implementa manejo de errores categorizado con prefijos UX_ERROR, NOT_FOUND y CAJA_CERRADA para respuestas HTTP apropiadas
- Todas las rutas estan protegidas con middleware verificarToken

Archivos modificados:
- src/controller/socioController.js: Adicion de 232 lineas con las tres nuevas funciones exportadas
- src/routes/socioRoutes.js: Importacion de nuevas funciones y registro de tres rutas POST/GET adicionales

author: mvillmow
body:
## Summary

- Add a runtime guard in `PrecisionConfig.bf16()` that raises a descriptive `Error` when called on Apple Silicon hardware, where `DType.bfloat16` is unsupported
- Extract the guard logic into a testable helper `_check_bf16_platform_support(is_apple: Bool)` so CI (Linux) can exercise the error path without Apple Silicon hardware
- Add new test file with 4 tests covering the guard behavior

## Changes Made

### `shared/training/precision_config.mojo`

- Added `from sys.info import is_apple_silicon` import
- Added `_check_bf16_platform_support(is_apple: Bool) raises` module-level helper
- Updated `bf16()` signature from `-> PrecisionConfig` to `raises -> PrecisionConfig`
- `bf16()` now calls `_check_bf16_platform_support(is_apple_silicon())` before constructing the config

### `tests/shared/training/test_bf16_apple_silicon_guard.mojo` (new)

- `test_check_bf16_platform_support_raises_on_apple`: Verifies guard raises with `is_apple=True`
- `test_check_bf16_platform_support_no_raise_on_non_apple`: Verifies guard passes with `is_apple=False`
- `test_bf16_succeeds_on_non_apple_silicon`: Verifies `PrecisionConfig.bf16()` succeeds on Linux CI
- `test_bf16_error_message_content`: Verifies error message mentions BF16, Apple Silicon, and `fp16()` alternative

## Design Decisions

- **Fail loudly**: Raises `Error` rather than silently falling back to FP16. Silent fallback would change semantics without warning and cause correctness bugs. Users who want FP16 should call `PrecisionConfig.fp16()` explicitly.
- **Testable helper**: The `_check_bf16_platform_support` helper accepts an `is_apple: Bool` argument so tests can exercise the error path on Linux CI without requiring Apple Silicon hardware.
- All existing callers of `bf16()` already have `raises` in their function signatures, so no other files needed updating.

## Verification

- All pre-commit hooks pass (mojo format, trailing whitespace, etc.)
- Existing tests are unaffected (all callers already propagate `raises`)
- Mojo tests must run in CI (Docker) due to GLIBC version incompatibility on local machine

Closes #3203

## Summary

Fixes 7 validated Codex review findings across deploy, config, soul, and bundle packages:

1. **host.ts (High)**: Store providers on `ManagedAgent`; rollback `attach()` on failure; call `provider.detach()` in `terminate()`, `terminateAll()`, and signal handlers — closes resource leak
2. **transcripting-engine (High)**: Map `senderId` to correct `TranscriptEntryRole` instead of hardcoding all inbound messages as `"user"`

6. **soul (Med-High)**: Match `_write` suffix instead of hardcoded `"fs_write"` so custom-prefixed write tools (e.g. `nx_write`) trigger auto-reload
7. **export-bundle (Medium)**: Propagate store I/O errors instead of masking all non-ok results as `NOT_FOUND`

author: sebetc4
body:
### Problem

When the 6.18 patch is applied using git apply (as opposed to the standard patch command), the kernel module snd-hda-scodec-aw88399 fails to build with:

`ERROR: modpost: missing MODULE_LICENSE() in sound/hda/codecs/side-codecs/snd-hda-scodec-aw88399.o`
This affects any build system that uses _git apply_ to apply patches, notably Fedora's _rpmbuild_/_fedpkg_ which defines _patch_command='git --work-tree=. apply'_ in _kernel.spec_.

Root causes
Two issues in the 6.18 patch cause _git apply_ to silently drop _MODULE_LICENSE("GPL");_ — the last line of _aw88399_hda.c_:

**1. Non-standard diff headers (_--color=auto_)**
The patch was generated using _diff --color=auto -u -r -N_, likely due to a shell alias. This embeds _'--color=auto'_ literally in the diff headers:


```
-diff '--color=auto' -u -r -N linux-6.18/sound/hda/codecs/...
+diff -u -r -N linux-6.18/sound/hda/codecs/...
```
While the standard _patch_ command tolerates these non-standard headers, _git apply_ does not properly recognize them as file boundaries and silently drops the last line of the preceding hunk.

**2. Incorrect hunk line count after Y9000P merge**
The merge adding Y9000P support (product 83F4, commit ab72a36) inserted a comment line in the _aw88399_hda.c_ hunk without updating the hunk header line count:


```
-@@ -0,0 +1,474 @@
+@@ -0,0 +1,475 @@
```
The hunk declared 474 added lines but contained 475. _git apply_ strictly respects the declared count and stops at line 474, dropping the 475th line: _MODULE_LICENSE("GPL");_.

### Fix
Remove _'--color=auto'_ from all diff headers
Correct the hunk line count: _474_ → _475_
No functional change to the patch content. The 6.19 patch is not affected by either issue.

author: calec
body:
## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive responsive design support to the desktop OS interface, enabling it to work seamlessly across mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints. The changes include a new `useBreakpoint` hook for detecting screen sizes, responsive window layouts, touch gesture support, and adaptive UI components.

## Key Changes

- **New `useBreakpoint` hook**: Added to `window.tsx`, `desktop.tsx`, and `taskbar.tsx` to detect screen size and return `isMobile` (< 768px), `isTablet` (768-1024px), and `isDesktop` (≥ 1024px) flags

- **Window component responsive behavior**:
  - Mobile: Windows slide up from bottom with `translateY` animation instead of scale
  - Mobile: Full-width layout with `calc(100vh - 40px)` height
  - Tablet: 90% width/height with 4% top and 5% left positioning
  - Desktop: Original draggable behavior with default sizing
  - Hide maximize/minimize buttons on mobile; show larger close button
  - Added touch swipe-down gesture on title bar to minimize (mobile/tablet only)

- **Desktop icon layout changes**:
  - Mobile: Vertical menu list with icon + label + arrow indicator
  - Tablet: Horizontal icon row at top
  - Desktop: Original vertical column layout on left side

- **Taskbar responsive adjustments**:
  - Mobile: Reduced padding/gaps and smaller font sizes
  - Mobile: Icon-only window buttons (fixed 36px width) instead of showing titles
  - Taskbar label changes from "CALE_OS" to "OS" on mobile

- **Projects window responsive grid**:
  - Mobile: Single column (name only)
  - Tablet/Desktop: Three columns (name, modified, size)
  - Hide "Modified" and "Size" columns on mobile using `display: ["none", "none", "block"]`

- **Skills window responsive layout**:
  - Stack vertically on mobile/tablet, side-by-side on desktop
  - Responsive gap sizing

- **Desktop icon interaction**:
  - Touch devices: Single tap opens window immediately
  - Desktop: Double-click to open, single-click to select (original behavior)

## Implementation Details

- All responsive breakpoints use consistent 768px (mobile) and 1024px (tablet) thresholds
- Window dragging is disabled on mobile/tablet and when maximized
- Touch event handlers use `useRef` to track swipe gestures
- Responsive values use Theme-UI array syntax for breakpoint-specific styling
- Mobile windows have reduced padding (12px vs 16px) and smaller fonts (12px vs 13px)

### Motivation
- Improve release confidence by adding deterministic runtime security probes, tying dependency CVE scans and SBOM evidence into the release gate, and surfacing tenant-isolation guardrails rather than only token-presence checks.
- Make screenshot capture provenance explicit so release artifacts cannot over-claim primary Playwright screenshots when fallback is used.
- Provide production guidance and enforcement knobs for Redis-backed rate limiting to avoid silent multi-instance drift.

### Description
- Added a runtime security smoke harness `scripts/security/runtime-smoke.mjs` and script entry `verify:security:runtime` that can launch a local app or target `--baseUrl`, probes security headers, rate-limit activation, and negative auth/tenant boundary behavior, and writes structured JSON at `artifacts/security/runtime-smoke/<run-id>/summary.json`.
- Implemented a supply-chain stage `scripts/security/supply-chain.mjs` with `verify:security:supply-chain` that runs `pnpm audit`, generates CycloneDX/SPDX SBOMs from `pnpm list --json`, emits a machine-readable summary, and records `auditUnavailableReason` when the registry audit endpoint is not usable.
- Added `scripts/verify-security-evidence.mjs` and `verify:security:evidence` to validate CI-provided supply-chain artifacts and enforce threshold failures in strict mode; CI job respects soft-skip policy via env toggles.
- Expanded `scripts/verify-security.mjs` to include static control checks, tenant-isolation guardrail evaluation (`scripts/security/tenant-guardrails.mjs`), and a production limiter backend guardrail; writes `artifacts/security/verify-security-summary.json` and emits actionable diagnostics.
- Hardened launch artifact capture (`scripts/capture-launch-assets.mjs`) and verification (`scripts/verify-launch-artifacts.mjs`) to include `origin` and `primaryFailure` metadata and to require that fallback runs document why primary capture failed.
- Added a production warning in the Redis-backed limiter (`packages/web/src/lib/security/rate-limiter-redis.ts`) when falling back to process-local counters in production, and documented behavior and enforcement options in `docs/security/RATE_LIMITING_PRODUCTION.md` and verification surfaces in `docs/security/VERIFICATION_SURFACES.md`.
- Wired the runner: `scripts/verify-release.mjs` gained `securityRuntime` and `securityEvidence` stages and the GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/release-verify.yml` now includes a `security-supply-chain` job that uploads artifacts and a release job that downloads and enforces evidence.
- Added unit tests for tenant guardrail evaluation (`scripts/__tests__/tenant-guardrails.test.mjs`) and new npm scripts in `package.json` for the new verification commands.

### Testing
- Ran `node --test scripts/__tests__/tenant-guardrails.test.mjs` and `pnpm run test:security:guardrails`; both tests passed.
- Executed `pnpm run verify:security` which produced `artifacts/security/verify-security-summary.json` and reported guardrail presence (passed in this environment where non-production limiter check is skipped).

author: dawoudio
body:
## Summary

A full cleanup of the 2FA settings architecture. The core idea: 2FA is a user security feature — every user should be able to self-enroll, and the system should handle all infrastructure automatically.

**Before:** 2FA required admins to manually configure an encryption key in `Config.php`, enable `bEnable2FA` to allow enrollment, and a separate `bRequire2FA` to mandate it. Enabling `bRequire2FA` hard-blocked all unenrolled users with "Invalid login or password".

**After:** The system auto-generates the encryption key on first boot (stored in DB, never exposed), `bEnable2FA` is removed entirely (enrollment is always available to all users), and `bRequire2FA` is the only admin control. Enabling it lets users log in and redirects them to enrollment on every request until they complete setup.

## Changes

### Core Authentication & Config

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `LoadConfigs.php` | Auto-generate `sTwoFASecretKey` unconditionally on boot — DB+ORM fully initialized before generation, persists immediately via Propel |
| `SystemConfig.php` | Remove `bEnable2FA`; remove Two-Factor Authentication settings category; add `password` type mapping |
| `LocalAuthentication.php` | Remove `getIsTwoFactorAuthSupported()`; 2FA prompt driven by enrollment status alone; `bRequire2FA` allows login then redirects to `/v2/user/current/manage2fa` on every request until enrolled |
| `AdminService.php` | Remove unreachable missing-key warning block |
| `UserService.php` | Remove `bEnable2FA` and `sTwoFASecretKey` from Quick Settings panel |

### API & Routes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `admin/routes/api/system/system-config.php` | **Add null checks before dereferencing config items** — prevents fatal error on unknown config names, returns 404; **Fix POST response contract** — return actual saved value for non-password types, empty string only for passwords |
| `v2/routes/user-current.php` | Remove dead auth provider branching (`instanceof LocalAuthentication` wrapper, unreachable SSO redirect, `unsupported-changepassword.php` reference); simplify to direct password change handler |
| `v2/templates/user/unsupported-2fa.php` | **Deleted** — enrollment is always supported |
| `v2/templates/common/unsupported-changepassword.php` | **Deleted** — dead code, no non-local auth providers exist |

### UI

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Header.php` | "Manage Two-Factor Authentication" always shown in user dropdown; `LocalAuthentication` import removed |
| `admin/views/users.php` | Removed Total Logins column; 2FA column always visible with `badge-success`/`badge-secondary` badges; Failed Logins badge only when >0; dropdown right-aligned |
| `system-settings-panel.js` | `password` type never fetches/displays value; blank with "Leave blank to keep existing" placeholder |
| `SettingsUser.php` | Cancel button navigates to `/admin/system/users` |

### Database & Docs

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mysql/upgrade/7.0.2-2fa.sql` | **New** — removes `bEnable2FA` from `config_cfg` |
| `src/mysql/upgrade.json` | Registers 7.0.2-2fa.sql in upgrade chain |
| `docs: secret-keys.md` | Rewritten as "Two-Factor Authentication" — covers auto-generated key, self-enrollment steps, `bRequire2FA` forced enrollment flow |
| `docs: faqs.md` | Removed obsolete "Secret Keys missing from Config.php" FAQ entry |
| `docs: administration/index.md` | Updated link label and description |
| `wiki: _Sidebar.md` | Updated link label to "Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)" |

### Testing & Infrastructure

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cypress/support/ui-commands.js` | Fix session `validate` callback — check server-side session validity via `/v2/dashboard` (200 = valid, 302 = expired) instead of browser cookie presence, preventing false positives when PHP sessions expire in long-running Docker containers |
| `cypress/e2e/api/private/admin/private.admin.system.config.spec.js` | **New** — comprehensive test suite for password-type config API protection: GET never exposes values, POST with empty value is a no-op, non-password POST returns saved value, unknown configs return 404 |

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh install: verify `sTwoFASecretKey` is auto-generated in DB on first page load
- [ ] "Manage Two-Factor Authentication" always appears in user dropdown (no admin flag required)
- [ ] User can self-enroll in 2FA without any admin config changes
- [ ] Enrolled user is prompted for TOTP code on next login
- [ ] Enable `bRequire2FA`: unenrolled users can log in, are redirected to enrollment page, and cannot access other pages until enrolled
- [ ] Complete enrollment with `bRequire2FA` on: redirect stops, normal access resumes
- [ ] `/v2/user/current/changepassword` works for local auth users (GET shows form, POST changes password)
- [ ] Quick Settings panel on `/admin/system/users` shows only `bRequire2FA` and `s2FAApplicationName`
- [ ] System Settings page has no "Two-Factor Authentication" category and no exposed secret key field
- [ ] Users table: 2FA column always visible with correct badges; failed logins badge only when >0
- [ ] DB upgrade: `bEnable2FA` removed from `config_cfg` after running 7.0.2-2fa.sql
- [ ] Config API password-type protection: run `npm run test:api -- --spec cypress/e2e/api/private/admin/private.admin.system.config.spec.js`

## Summary
Refactored the depth milestone sound effect to play from the banner display method instead of the zone transition check method, improving code organization and preventing duplicate sound plays.

## Key Changes
- Removed `SoundManager.play_depth_milestone_sound()` call from `_check_zone_transition()` method
- Added `SoundManager.play_depth_milestone_sound()` call to `_show_zone_banner()` method at the start of execution

## Implementation Details
This change ensures the depth milestone sound plays once per banner display rather than potentially multiple times during zone transition logic. By moving the sound call to `_show_zone_banner()`, the sound is now gated by the banner's cooldown mechanism (`COOLDOWN_MS`), preventing rapid successive sound plays and creating a more polished audio experience during zone transitions.

### Motivation
- Reduce coupling by centralizing all network interactions and moving pure numeric formulas out of the main component for easier testing and maintenance. 
- Separate concerns so authentication, data access, and derived calculations are reusable and easier to reason about. 
- Shrink `App.jsx` responsibility to a high-level orchestrator and extract large visual sections to dedicated components for clarity. 

### Description
- Added a centralized API client at `frontend/src/services/apiClient.js` that encapsulates all `fetch` calls behind semantic methods like `login`, `getLatestArqueo`, `saveArqueo`, reporting and saldos endpoints. 
- Introduced hooks to split logic: `hooks/useAuth.js` (login state/flow), `hooks/useArqueoData.js` (API exposure), and `hooks/useArqueoCalculations.js` (memoized derived calculations). 
- Moved pure numeric logic into `frontend/src/domain/arqueoMath.js` with functions `calcBilletesTotal`, `calcSumaIngresosBancos`, `calcSafeDiff` and `calcCajaMayorMovs`. 
- Extracted large visual blocks into components `ArqueoHeader`, `ArqueoActionsBar`, `ArqueoTables`, and `ReportView`, and updated `App.jsx` to orchestrate these pieces while preserving existing save, navigation, delete/undo and reporting flows. 
- Updated `components/Login.jsx` to use the centralized `apiClient` for consistency. 

### Testing
- Built the frontend with `npm run build` (Vite) and the build completed successfully. 
- Started the dev server and captured a runtime screenshot via Playwright to validate the UI renders after the refactor.

author: copilot
body:
`_build_detailed_daily_data()` initialised `prev_evening_fuel = None`, so when no in-month fuel log events existed the entire month showed `—` for all fuel columns — even when the DB already held a valid `current_fuel` opening balance.

## Changes

### `reports/excel_reports.py`
- Before the day loop, read `current_fuel` from `db.get_state()` and use it as the initial `prev_evening_fuel` seed:

```python
initial_fuel: float | None = None
try:
    state_fuel = db.get_state().get("current_fuel")
    if state_fuel is not None:
        parsed = float(state_fuel)
        if parsed > 0:
            initial_fuel = parsed
except Exception:
    pass

prev_evening_fuel: float | None = initial_fuel
```

- `corr_fuel_set` events on any day still take priority (existing logic untouched)
- DB value of `0` or missing → falls back to `None` (no regression on fresh/empty state)
- Subsequent days continue propagating from the previous day's evening balance as before

### `tests/test_excel_reports.py`
Added `TestDetailedReportOpeningFuelSeed` covering:
- Day 1 morning/evening reflects DB `current_fuel` when no in-month events exist
- Day 1 evening correctly applies refill and consumption on top of the seeded value
- `corr_fuel_set` on day 1 overrides the DB seed (manual correction takes priority)
- Day 2 morning equals day 1 evening (seed propagates forward correctly)
- DB fuel = 0 falls back to `—` placeholder (no regression)
- Other report types (quick/technical/financial/personnel) are unaffected

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Implement a focused fix in repository imeromua/generator_bot for the upgraded Analytics -> Detailed monthly Excel report.
> 
> Problem:
> The new detailed monthly report does not account for the opening fuel balance stored in the database/state on the 1st day of the month. Right now `_build_detailed_daily_data()` starts with `prev_evening_fuel = None` and derives fuel balances only from in-month log events (`corr_fuel_set`, previous propagated balance, or first refill). As a result, when the database already contains a known current fuel balance for the first day of the month, the report can show an incorrect or missing starting balance.
> 
> Concrete user case:
> - For March 1, the opening balance should be 69 liters.
> - That value exists in the database.
> - The Detailed report must use that DB value as the opening fuel balance for the month.
> 
> Goal:
> Make the Detailed monthly workbook seed fuel calculations from the opening fuel value stored in DB/state for the 1st day of the report month.
> 
> Requirements:
> 1. Data source
> - Find the existing DB/state source that stores the current fuel amount / current fuel balance.
> - Reuse the project’s existing DB/state API if available (for example state-related getters or generator-specific state/config if that is where the value lives).
> - Do not hardcode 69; this is only an example proving the missing behavior.
> 
> 2. Fuel calculation behavior
> - For the first calendar day of the detailed report month, initialize the fuel chain from the DB opening balance.
> - This opening value should populate the first day’s morning/start balance logic.
> - Then apply that day’s refills and consumption to compute the first day’s ending balance.
> - Subsequent days should continue using the existing propagation logic from previous day to next day.
> 
> 3. Priority / override rules
> - If there is an explicit manual correction event for the same day (`corr_fuel_set`), treat it as authoritative for the corrected balance on that day.
> - Preserve existing manual correction behavior.
> - The new opening-balance seed should fill the gap when there is no in-month anchor before/at the start of the month.
> 
> 4. Scope
> - Change only the Detailed monthly report behavior unless a small shared helper is the cleanest way.
> - Do not break quick/technical/financial/personnel reports.
> - Keep Detailed report current-month behavior exactly as it is now.
> 
> 5. Workbook expectations
> - After the fix, the main operational sheet and monthly summary sheet should reflect the correct first-day fuel opening balance.
> - Example expectation: if DB opening fuel on March 1 is 69 L, the first day should begin from 69 L before applying that day’s consumption/refills unless overridden by a manual correction.
> 
> 6. Tests
> Add/extend tests covering:
> - Detailed report seeds first day from DB opening fuel.
> - Manual correction event still overrides appropriately.
> - First-day morning/evening values are recalculated correctly from DB seed + consumption/refill.
> - Existing detailed-report structure/formatting tests remain green.
> 
> Deliverable:
> A PR that fixes the opening fuel balance issue in the detailed monthly Excel report so the report becomes accurate from the first day of the month when DB already has the starting fuel balance.


</details>

body:
## Summary Fixes 4 issues found during a cross-repo docs audit. The original audit identified 5 fix groups, but investigation showed Fix Group 1 (JSON Schema gaps) was a false positive for the runtime schema — the package schema was already correct. Only the repo-root copy was stale. ### Changes - **Sync `schemas/edictum-v1.schema.json`** — the repo-root copy was missing SandboxContract, approve effect, observability section, and observe_alongside. The runtime schema (in `src/edictum/yaml_engine/`) was already correct, which is why sandbox contracts work fine. Copied package schema to repo root. - **Remove OTel `team` ghost** — `__init__.py:1610` iterated over `("role", "team", ...)` but `Principal` has no `team` field. `audit_event.principal.get("team")` always returned `None`, making it a silent no-op that misleads OTel span readers. Removed `"team"` from the loop. - **Nanobot `is_error` check** — `nanobot.py:_check_tool_success()` was missing the `isinstance(result, dict) / result.get("is_error")` check that all 7 other adapters have. Dict results with `{"is_error": true}` were incorrectly treated as successful. - **`run()` default success heuristic** — `Edictum.run()` defaulted to `tool_success = True` when no `success_check` was provided, while all 8 adapters apply a heuristic (None/dict/str checks). Added `_default_success_check()` so `run()` behavior matches adapters. ### What was NOT done (and why) - **Fix Group 1 (schema rewrite)** — false positive. The runtime schema already has all features. Only the repo-root copy needed syncing. - **Fix Group 5 (observe mode callback gap)** — intentional by design. In global observe mode, the tool executes as if governance didn't exist, so neither `on_deny` nor `on_allow` fires. This is correct semantics. - **Adapter refactor** — did not extract adapters' `_check_tool_success` into a shared function. LangChain, Google ADK, and Semantic Kernel have adapter-specific extensions (ToolMessage content, `error` key, FunctionResult metadata), so a shared base would still need per-adapter overrides. Not worth the churn. ## Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/` — 1800 passed, 3 skipped - [x] `edictum validate src/edictum/yaml_engine/templates/*.yaml` — all 4 templates valid - [x] `ruff check` — clean - [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, ruff-format, check-terminology)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes four correctness issues found during a cross-repo audit: syncing the stale repo-root JSON Schema, removing a ghost OTel span attribute, adding a missing `is_error` dict check in the nanobot adapter, and aligning `Edictum.run()`'s default success heuristic with all framework adapters. - **Schema sync** (`schemas/edictum-v1.schema.json`): Verified identical to `src/edictum/yaml_engine/edictum-v1.schema.json` post-PR via diff. Adds `SandboxContract`, `Observability`, `observe_alongside`, `approve` effect, `timeout`/`timeout_effect` on `Then`, and relaxes `Operator.additionalProperties` to `{}` to allow custom operators — all already present and working in the runtime schema. - **OTel ghost field** (`__init__.py:1610`): `"team"` correctly removed from the principal attribute loop. `Principal` has fields `user_id`, `service_id`, `org_id`, `role`, `ticket_ref`, `claims` — no `team` field, confirming the prior iteration was a silent no-op. - **Nanobot `is_error`** (`nanobot.py:_check_tool_success`): The `isinstance(result, dict) / result.get("is_error")` guard is now in place, correctly positioned before the string heuristic, matching all other adapters. - **`run()` success heuristic** (`__init__.py:_default_success_check`): The new module-level `_default_success_check()` correctly replicates the adapter heuristic — `None → True`, dict with truthy `is_error → False`, string prefixed `error:`/`fatal: → False`, everything else `→ True`. Logic is consistent with `nanobot._check_tool_success()` and the `tool_name` parameter is carried for API signature parity with user-provided `_success_check` callables.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge — all four fixes are narrow, well-reasoned, and backed by 1800 passing tests. - Each change is a clear bug fix with no new logic complexity: the schema sync is verified identical to the already-working runtime schema; the OTel removal is confirmed by inspecting the Principal dataclass; the nanobot dict guard matches the pattern across all other adapters; and _default_success_check mirrors the same logic already battle-tested in every adapter. No regressions are expected. - No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | schemas/edictum-v1.schema.json | Syncs repo-root schema to runtime schema: adds SandboxContract, Observability, observe_alongside, approve effect, timeout/timeout_effect to Then, and relaxes Operator additionalProperties from false to {} to support custom operators. Verified identical to src/edictum/yaml_engine/edictum-v1.schema.json post-PR. | | src/edictum/__init__.py | Two targeted fixes: (1) removes the ghost "team" key from the OTel principal attribute loop (Principal has no team field), (2) adds _default_success_check() module-level function so Edictum.run() applies the same None/dict/str heuristic as all 8 adapters instead of defaulting to True. | | src/edictum/adapters/nanobot.py | Adds the missing isinstance(result, dict)/result.get("is_error") check to GovernedToolRegistry._check_tool_success(), aligning it with all 7 other adapters. The fix is placed correctly before the string heuristic check. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A["Edictum.run(tool_name, result)"] --> B{_success_check provided?} B -- Yes --> C["user _success_check(tool_name, result)"] B -- No --> D["_default_success_check(tool_name, result) ← NEW"] D --> E{result is None?} E -- Yes --> F["return True ✓"] E -- No --> G{isinstance result dict?} G -- Yes --> H{"result.get('is_error') truthy?"} H -- Yes --> I["return False ✗"] H -- No --> J{isinstance result str?} G -- No --> J J -- Yes --> K{"starts with 'error:' or 'fatal:'?"} K -- Yes --> L["return False ✗"] K -- No --> M["return True ✓"] J -- No --> M subgraph "nanobot._check_tool_success (same heuristic)" N["result is None?"] --> O["True ✓"] N --> P["dict is_error?"] --> Q["False ✗"] N --> R["str error:/fatal:?"] --> S["False ✗"] N --> T["else True ✓"] end ``` Last reviewed commit: cd67bf0

body:
### Motivation
- Unify and extend inventory to support multiple measurement units and reliable conversions so stock/thresholds work for both weight and unitary measures.
- Improve expiry visibility with per-entry badges and lists so soon-to-expire and expired lots are clearer in lists and tables.
- Allow per-product package quantities and preserve unit choice across entries to prevent inconsistent data entry.
- Surface provider contact info and make measure selection compatible with ingredient preferred unit to reduce user errors.

### Description
- Added unit metadata and conversion helpers (`getUnitMeta`, `toBase`, `fromBase`, `formatQtyUnit`) and track per-record `stockBase` / `stockUnit` plus `availableBase`/`qtyBase` on entries to compute consistent totals across units. 
- Reworked stock/threshold logic (`recomputeRecordStock`, `currentThresholdFor`, `stockStatusFor`) to operate on base quantities and support a `lowThresholdMode` (global/custom) and a new global `globalLowThresholdUnits` config.
- Introduced package quantity support (`packageQty`) with UI controls and validation to lock or enforce package counts for an ingredient, and prevent adding incompatible units to existing ingredients.
- Enhanced expiry UX with `getDaysUntilIso`, `getExpiryBadgeTone`, `getExpiryBadgeHtml`, `inventario-expiring-list` rendering for soon/expired rows, `inventario-expired-strike` styling, and per-entry expiry badges in lists and tables.
- Replaced single `day kg` calendar bubbles with a summary that shows mixed `kg + units` using `getDaySummaryMap` and new CSS class `inventario-day-kg.is-mixed` for display variants.
- Provider model extended with `email` and `phone`, provider creation/edit flows updated to capture these fields, and provider cards updated to show contact info.
- Recipes/production updated to understand the expanded unit vocabulary and convert/display units consistently (`getUnitMeta` additions, `toComparableQuantity` updates, measure-select now disables incompatible measures via `getCompatibleMeasureOptions`).
- Pagination and expand/collapse logic in several inventory-expanded views updated to page expanded results and fix collapse/expand semantics, and multiple UI texts and table headers adjusted to show `Cantidad`/unit instead of only kilos.
- Styling and layout tweaks including new classes (`inventario-expiring-list`, `inventario-expiring-line`, `inventario-expiry-days-badge`, `inventario-expired-strike`) and modal size increased from `modal-lg` to `modal-xl` for large dialogs in `index.html`.

### Testing

author: hardonian
body:
### Motivation
- Close and make machine-evident outstanding launch security gaps (dependency triage, route classification, admin auth/authz, error-path header/CSP, RLS proof) while preserving truthful boundaries where runtime/external inputs are required.
- Prefer minimal, reviewer-friendly changes that add deterministic checks, artifacts, and explicit failure modes rather than suppressing or hiding issues.

### Description
- Added a route classification model and richer coverage diagnostics in `scripts/security/tenant-guardrails.mjs` and surfaced those in `scripts/verify-security.mjs` so coverage now reports `classificationCoveragePct`, `categoryCounts`, `manualReviewRoutes`, and exact `unclassifiedRoutes`.
- Added static admin auth/authz verifier `scripts/security/admin-route-authz.mjs` to scan `/api/admin/**/route.ts` for `isSuperAdmin`/`requireSuperAdmin`, denial semantics, security wrapper usage, and denial cache-control hints, and authored artifact outputs under `artifacts/security/*` and `security/evidence/admin-route-authz.json`.
- Expanded header/CSP probing in `scripts/security/header-probe.mjs` to: probe probeable API routes, special-paths (not-found, denial path, admin redirect), include expectation modes, and emit detailed per-route failures in `artifacts/security/header-probe/*` and `security/evidence/header-probe.json`.
- Added dependency triage script `scripts/security/dependency-triage.mjs` that builds `security/dependency-triage.json` (canonical disposition), records a blocking sentinel when a Dependabot export is missing, and captures audit artifact presence and known outstanding count (22 in this environment).
- Introduced RLS proof-level boundary script `scripts/security/verify-rls-boundary.mjs` that attempts `scripts/verify-rls-status.ts` when DB credentials are present and emits `static-only | live-db-confirmed | live-db-attempted-failed` artifacts under `artifacts/security/rls-verification/*` and `security/evidence/rls-verification.json`.
- Extended evidence packper `scripts/security-evidence.mjs` to include the new artifacts (admin authz, dependency-triage, rls-verification) and to mark degraded/partial completeness explicitly in `security/evidence/security-summary.*` and `security/evidence/manifest.json`.
- Fixed `scripts/security-drift-check.mjs` (`listDiff` undefined) and added baseline update behavior; updated tests to reflect classification behavior in `scripts/__tests__/tenant-guardrails.test.mjs`.
- Minor `package.json` script wiring so `verify:security` and `security:evidence` run the new checks and artifact generation.

Files added or modified (high level): `scripts/security/admin-route-authz.mjs`, `scripts/security/dependency-triage.mjs`, `scripts/security/verify-rls-boundary.mjs`, `scripts/security/header-probe.mjs` (updated), `scripts/security/tenant-guardrails.mjs` (updated), `scripts/security-evidence.mjs` (updated), `scripts/security-drift-check.mjs` (fixed), `scripts/__tests__/tenant-guardrails.test.mjs` (updated), `package.json` (scripts), plus generated artifacts under `security/` and `artifacts/security/`.

### Testing
- Ran unit/regression tests: `node --test scripts/__tests__/tenant-guardrails.test.mjs` — PASS (all tests passed after test update).
- Lint/type/build: `pnpm lint` — PASS with warnings; `pnpm typecheck` — PASS; `pnpm build` — PASS (web build completed and produced routes).
- Route & tenant checks: `pnpm run security:routes` and `pnpm run verify:tenant` — PASS; produced `security/route-registry.json` and `artifacts/security/tenant-coverage-latest.json` with 100% token-presence coverage.
- Cross-tenant runtime tests: `pnpm run test:cross-tenant` — PASS (3 suites, 11 tests passed).
- Admin auth verifier: `node scripts/security/admin-route-authz.mjs` — PASS and produced `security/evidence/admin-route-authz.json` (9 admin routes, passed with warnings recorded).
- Header/CSP probe: `pnpm run verify:security:headers` / `node scripts/security/header-probe.mjs` — completed and produced `security/evidence/header-probe.json`, but shows real failures: `passed: 0, failed: 136` (missing CSP / x-request-id and missing denial cache-control on many error/denial paths); this is surfaced intentionally for remediation.
- Dependency audit & triage: `pnpm run audit:deps` returned `warn-backend-unavailable` in this environment (pnpm audit backend returned 403 and `osv-scanner` absent); `node scripts/security/dependency-triage.mjs` produced `security/dependency-triage.json` with an explicit blocker `dependabot-export-missing` and known outstanding count `22` (triage incomplete but machine-evident).
- RLS boundary: `node scripts/security/verify-rls-boundary.mjs` — run in this environment with no DB credentials, produced `rls-verification` artifact with `proofLevel: static-only` and clear boundary messaging; if DB credentials are provided later the script will attempt a live verification and upgrade the proof level.
- Evidence composition: `SECURITY_BASELINE_UPDATE=1 pnpm run security:evidence` — PASS and generated `security/evidence/*` artifacts and updated baseline; `scripts/security-drift-check.mjs` baseline update ran successfully.

Notes on outcomes and next steps:
- Dependency triage is now machine-recorded but requires an authenticated Dependabot export (`security/dependabot-alerts.json`) to complete the per-CVE dispositions; artifact explicitly blocks/records this gap.
- Header/CSP failures are real findings surfaced in artifacts and should be remediated or triaged into rules that explain acceptable exceptions; current CI policy keeps these visible rather than masking them.
- Live RLS confirmation is intentionally gated by DB credentials; the new verifier makes the boundary explicit so CI/staging can be configured to run live verification when appropriate.

This change set makes the security verification pipeline materially more rigorous and machine-evident while keeping honest boundaries where runtime or external service access is required.

author: pdaian
body:
### Motivation

- Incoming Signal group events sometimes lack a human-readable title, producing unreadable conversation identifiers. 
- The client should prefer readable group names when available and fall back to a cached name when the live event omits the title. 
- Cache group metadata similarly to contacts to reduce subprocess calls and improve display consistency.

### Description

- Added a new `groups_command` parameter with a default `['signal-cli','-o','json','-a',account,'listGroups']` and internal caches `_group_names` and `_group_names_loaded_at` in `SignalClient`.
- Refresh group metadata during `get_updates()` by calling a new helper `_refresh_group_cache_if_needed` and parse JSON output with `_parse_groups_output`/`_parse_group_payload`.
- Updated `_extract_group_title` to record titles into the group cache and changed `_build_group_conversation_id` to prefer a live title, then the cached name, while still including the group id in the returned `group:<name>|<id>` form.
- Extended `tests/test_signal_client.py` to account for the extra `listGroups` subprocess call, added `test_uses_cached_group_name_when_message_lacks_group_title`, and adjusted contact-cache TTL test timing to include group-cache checks.

### Testing

- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_signal_client.py` with `PYTHONPATH=.`, and all tests passed: `17 passed`.
- A raw `pytest` run without `PYTHONPATH` initially failed during collection with `ModuleNotFoundError`, which was resolved by running tests with `PYTHONPATH=.`.
- The modified test suite includes the new cache/fallback coverage and confirms existing behavior for contacts, message parsing, and sending remains unchanged.

💡 **What:** Replaced the `.filter().find()` chain in `src/core/statecharts/core-logic/visualizer-template.ts` with a single `.find()` operation that short-circuits.
🎯 **Why:** The previous code filtered `candidateTransitions` into a new array and then called `find()` to evaluate the guard conditions. This caused unnecessary array allocations and iterations.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Running a benchmark script with 100,000 transitions over 1,000 iterations showed the original `.filter().find()` taking ~2357ms, while the optimized `.find()` took ~0.3ms. This demonstrates a massive reduction in unnecessary loops and array allocation overhead.

author: ygifoom
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a reusable, resumable, stage-based lane-1 pipeline for structure-based binder design that can run stages as separate RunAI jobs with site-specific container images and PVC mounts. 
- Standardize stage interfaces, on-disk artifacts, and hotspot extraction by making RFdiffusion JSON the primary hotspot source. 
- Ship a lightweight Python orchestrator, stage command templates, cluster submit helpers, and documentation to simplify launching and resuming multi-stage runs on EPFL RCP / RunAI.

### Description
- Introduces a new `pipeline` package implementing config parsing (`pipeline/config.py`), a simple YAML loader (`pipeline/simple_yaml.py`), hotspot loading (`pipeline/hotspots.py`), RunAI job builder (`pipeline/runai.py`), orchestrator (`pipeline/orchestrator.py`), stage contract helpers (`pipeline/stage_contract.py`), stage definitions (`pipeline/stages.py`), and per-stage shell script generators (`pipeline/stage_commands.py`).
- Adds cluster templates and example job submit scripts under `cluster/templates/` and a top-level launcher script `scripts/run_pipeline.sh` that writes a temporary YAML config and calls the orchestrator. 
- Provides presets and example configs `configs/lane1.fast.yaml` and `configs/lane1.thorough.yaml`, documentation for hotspot and output schemas under `docs/`, a detailed `README.md`, and example/manual hotspot YAML under `examples/`.
- Adds unit tests exercising config/hotspot parsing, orchestrator dry-run behavior, stage command generation, and stage lifecycle contract, plus a `.gitignore` and `requirements.txt` with `PyYAML` dependency. 

### Testing
- Added unit tests: `tests/test_config_and_hotspots.py`, `tests/test_orchestrator_dry_run.py`, `tests/test_stage_commands.py`, and `tests/test_stage_contract.py` to validate config loading, hotspot parsing, dry-run orchestration behavior, stage-script content, and stage lifecycle contract. 
- Ran the test suite with `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and all tests completed successfully. 
- Dry-run behavior of the orchestrator was validated via mocks to ensure it does not create host scratch directories when `--dry-run` or `PIPELINE_LOCAL_STATE=0`.

body:
This fixes the INT8 calibrator preprocessing for 3-channel input.

  `calibrator.cpp` currently uses `offsets[3]` for the third channel:
  `cv::Scalar(offsets[0] / 255, offsets[1] / 255, offsets[3] / 255)`

  The sample configs define three offsets, so the third value should be `offsets[2]`.

  This change only affects the INT8 calibration path.

- Evita adicionar `X-CSRF-Token` quando o chamador já forneceu um header `x-csrf-token` em outra capitalização.
- Adiciona um teste em `src/services/apiClient.test.js` cobrindo o cenário onde o chamador envia `content-type` e `x-csrf-token` em minúsculas.

author: copilot
body:
Client-submitted devis were invisible to the owner on other devices because `_save()` fired a one-shot fetch with no retry — silent failures left data only in device-local localStorage. There was also no notification mechanism when a new devis arrived.

## Storage sync (`src/utils/storage.js`)
- `_save()` now tracks an async `_postWithRetry()` chain: up to 3 attempts at 1s / 2s / 4s backoff
- Failed writes are queued in `paradise_retry_queue` (localStorage) so they survive page reloads
- Exported sync status API: `getSyncStatus()`, `onSyncStatusChange()`, `offSyncStatusChange()`, `retryFailedWrites()`
- Added `notifyNewDevis(devis)` — fire-and-forget POST to `/api/notify.php`

## Sync indicator (`src/components/SyncIndicator.jsx` + `src/App.jsx`)
Floating bottom-right widget (z-index 9999) with three states:
- 🔄 Spinning — write in progress
- ✅ Green — all synced (auto-hides after 3 s)
- ⚠️ Red — offline, data saved locally, with a **Réessayer** button that drains the retry queue

## Email notification (`api/notify.php` + `api/config.php`)
New PHP endpoint called from `Step7Summary` after `saveClients()`:
```php
// api/config.php
return [
    'admin_email' => 'contact@leparadise77.fr',
    'site_name'   => 'LE PARADISE',
    'site_url'    => 'https://leparadise77.fr',
];
```
Sends an HTML email (client name/email/phone, event type/date/guests, devis number, total TTC, dashboard link). `$siteName` is CRLF-stripped and MIME-encoded before use in headers to prevent header injection; `$adminEmail` is validated via `filter_var`.

## Document sync (`src/components/EspaceClient/EspaceClient.jsx`)
- `saveDocs()` now also POSTs to `/api/storage.php` under key `paradise_docs_{devisId}`
- On mount, `fetchDocsFromServer()` hydrates state from the server (with a cancellation guard on `devisId` changes to prevent stale-response races)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Context

This is a React + Vite + PHP app for "Le Paradise" event venue. It has a quote (devis) wizard, a client area, and an admin dashboard. Data is stored via an in-memory cache → localStorage → PHP server file storage system (`api/storage.php` saves JSON files to `api/data/`).

**Problem**: When a client submits a devis from their phone, it is not visible in the dashboard on another device (e.g., the owner's computer). The server-side storage (`api/storage.php`) is silently failing and the app falls back to localStorage which is device-local. There is also no notification system — the owner has no way to know when a new devis comes in.

## Changes Required

### 1. Fix data synchronization (storage.js)

In `src/utils/storage.js`, the `_save()` function currently does a fire-and-forget `fetch()` POST to the PHP server with only a `console.warn` on failure. This needs to be improved:

**a) Add retry logic with exponential backoff:**
- If the POST to `/api/storage.php` fails, retry up to 3 times with increasing delays (1s, 2s, 4s).
- Keep a queue of failed writes and retry them periodically.

**b) Add a visible sync status indicator:**
- Export a `getSyncStatus()` function and an event system so UI components can show sync state.
- Track pending writes, successful syncs, and failures.
- Expose a `onSyncStatusChange(callback)` / `offSyncStatusChange(callback)` API.

**c) Add a `SyncIndicator` React component** in `src/components/SyncIndicator.jsx`:
- Show a small floating indicator in the bottom-right corner of the screen.
- Green dot + "✅ Synchronisé" when all data is synced.
- Orange spinning + "🔄 Synchronisation..." when writes are in progress.
- Red dot + "⚠️ Hors ligne — données sauvées localement" when the server is unreachable, with a "Réessayer" button.
- Style it consistently with the app (dark theme `#1a1a2e`, gold accent `#c9a84c`).

**d) Add this `SyncIndicator` to `src/App.jsx`** so it appears on all pages.

**e) Add `await` to the server persist in `_save()`:**
- Make `_save()` return a Promise.
- The existing code makes _save synchronous for the cache and localStorage, then fires off the server POST. Keep this pattern but track the Promise for the retry queue.

### 2. Add email notification when a new devis is submitted

**a) Create `api/notify.php`:**
- A PHP endpoint that receives a POST with JSON body containing devis details.
- Sends an email using PHP's `mail()` function to the configured admin email.
- The email should be an HTML email with a nice format including:
  - Client name, email, phone
  - Event type, date, number of guests
  - Devis number
  - Total TTC amount
  - A link to the dashboard
- Use the same CORS headers pattern as `api/storage.php`.
- Admin email should be configurable — read it from a `api/config.php` file that returns the admin email. Create this file with a default value of `contact@leparadise77.fr`.
- Return `{"success": true}` on success, `{"error": "..."}` on failure.

**b) Create `api/config.php`:**
```php
<?php
return [
    'admin_email' => 'contact@leparadise77.fr',
    'site_name' => 'LE PARADISE',
    'site_url' => 'https://leparadise77.fr',
];
```

**c) Add a `notifyNewDevis(devis)` function in `src/utils/storage.js`:**
- Makes a POST to `/api/notify.php` with the devis data.
- Fire and forget — don't block the UI, but log errors.

**d) Call `notifyNewDevis(devis)` in `src/components/Wizard/steps/Step7Summary.jsx`:**
- After `saveClients(...)` is called in the `handleSubmit()` function, also call `notifyNewDevis(devis)`.
- Import it from storage.js.

### 3. Fix documents storage (EspaceClient.jsx)

In `src/components/EspaceClient/EspaceClient.jsx`, the `getDocs()` and `saveDocs()` functions use **only localStorage** and never sync to the server. This means documents uploaded by clients are never visible from other devices.

**Fix:** Update `saveDocs()` to also POST to the PHP server using the same pattern as `_save()` in storage.js, using the key `paradise_docs_{devisId}`. And update `getDocs()` to first try fetching from the server on initial load.

### Important implementation notes:

- The PHP server stores data in `api/data/` as JSON files.
- The vite dev proxy forwards `/api` to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
- Keep all existing functionality working.
- All UI text should be in French.
- The retry queue should persist failed writes in localStorage so they survive page reloads.
- The SyncIndicator should have a z-index high enough to float above other content.

### Files to modify:
- `src/utils/storage.js` — retry logic, sync status, notifyNewDevis function
- `src/components/SyncIndicator.jsx` — new file, sync status UI component
- `src/App.jsx` — add SyncIndicator
- `src/components/Wizard/steps/Step7Summary.jsx` — call notifyNewDevis after devis creation
- `src/components/EspaceClient/EspaceClient.jsx` — fix docs sync
- `api/notify.php` — new file, email notification endpoint
- `api/config.php` — new file, admin configuration

author: begetan
body:
## Problem

ArcFace face recognition (`model_size: large`) produces wrong person labels
at 99-100% confidence on RK3588 with RKNN detector. All faces — including
non-face objects — are assigned the same label. The issue does not occur on
AMD/ROCm or CPU builds.

## Root cause

`RKNNModelRunner.run()` passes `float32 NCHW` tensors to `rknn.inference()`
for the ArcFace `"data"` input. The compiled `arcface.rknn` model has
`mean_values=[[127.5,127.5,127.5]]` and `std_values=[[127.5,127.5,127.5]]`
baked in at conversion time, meaning the RKNN runtime expects `uint8 NHWC
[0,255]` and applies `(x - 127.5) / 127.5` internally.

When pre-normalised `float32 [-1,+1]` arrives instead, the runtime applies
the normalisation a second time, collapsing the effective input range from
`[-1,+1]` to `[-1.008, -0.992]` — a 125x compression. Every embedding
produced is near-constant regardless of input.

The `pixel_values` (CLIP/Jina) branch in the same method already handles
the NCHW→NHWC transpose correctly. The `"data"` (ArcFace) branch was missing
the equivalent conversion.

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
